string.text: Hail there traveller, might I borrow a moment of your time?
What can i do for you?

I am Philo, of Byzantium, a learned man and author of “De septem orbis miraculis”, a novel whose purpose is singular; to bring the might and beauty of man’s greatest architectural achievements to all who read it.

You see, I have gathered some knowledge about these sights from many ancient authors, but I have never seen them for myself. So i'm looking for someone who'll visit each wonder and give a detailed account of them. Interested?
Indeed, my journey is sure to take me eastward. I can certainly visit those wonders for you!
Splendid! I will pay you well once you've returned with the accounts of all the seven wonders! Good luck on your travels!
Tell me about the Great Pyramid!

The construction of the Pyramids at Memphis is beyond the strength of men and their description is beyond belief, for they are mountains placed on top of mountains, and it is not easy for the mind to grasp how the huge masses of hewn stone could have been raised; and all have doubts concerning the huge force of the mechanical devices needed to bring the massive structures together!
Tell me about the Hanging Gardens of Babylon!

The Hanging Garden suspends its plants in the air, having shoots which are supported away from the ground. The tree roots which hang above the ground, assuredly cover the earth and take the place of a floor. Here grow grasses which are perennially green, and trees whose leaves move in the breeze. The branches are made soft by constant moisture and so the leaves grow more densely. The roots, which are never removed, exude water continuously, and this circulates through the pores of the roots which are buried and pressed into the ground, keeping the trees naturally firm and thick. And so the cultivator, in his many ways, has created strength through nature; this certainly is a work of regal splendour giving much pleasure suspended above the heads of onlookers.
Tell me about the Colossus of Rhodus!

You can still see the feet of the mighty Colossus, the rest of the body collapsed hundreds of years ago when an earthquake shook the island...The artist used so much bronze for the work that there was almost a shortage of metals, for all the earth’s mines were exploited in carrying out the project. You will remember that Zeus deluged the Rhodians with great wealth so that they might devote it to honouring the Sun as they had undertaken to produce a statue of the god that would stretch right from the earth to the sky. The workmen fortified the statue of the Colossus from the inside by hewn stones joined together by iron bolts, and the bars which are used on the stones to bring the joins together seem to have been fashioned by the hammers of the Cyclops. Whatever part of the work remains hidden is greater than that which can be seen; for the onlooker, transfixed in admiration, can only doubt that such vast masses of bronze could have been melted down and cast, wonder by what clamps they have been held, to what kind of blows they have been subjected and what strenuous exertions have brought them into being.
Tell me about Statue of Zeus!

As Kronos is Zeus’s father in heaven, so Phidias is his father in Elis. Immortal nature gave birth to the former, but the hands of Phidias, which alone have satisfied the gods, begat the latter. Blessed is Phidias who, alone, has seen the king of the world and has re-created his awesome presence for all to see. If it belittles Zeus to call him the son of Phidias, might we still not consider his mother to be Art, by which means Phidias created Zeus’s likeness. We honour the other Wonders of the World with our admiration, but this is the only one that we venerate. For however much a work of art is to be admired, the image of Zeus is sacrosanct. If labour is worthy of praise, then an immortal being must truly be worthy of reverence
Tell me about the Temple of Artemis!

The unique Temple of Artemis at Ephesos is the abode of gods. Whoever has gazed upon it will believe that the heavenly world of the immortals has changed places with the earth. The Giants, or Aloidae, who undertook to conquer Olympus with mountains, have now built not a temple but a dwelling fit for gods. Just as work in progress surpasses its foundation, so art, by its boldness, surpasses the work in progress. The artist, isolated from everyone because his work was known only to him, dug trenches to an immense depth and exhausted the mountain quarries in laying his extensive foundations.
Tell me about the Pharos of Alexandria!

Legend has it that the people of the island of Pharos were wreckers; hence, Ptolemaios I Soter had the lighthouse built to help guide ships into port at night! It is said to be the tallest tower of the world, it's light visible over thirty miles!
Tell me about the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus!

It is likely that Mausolus started to plan the tomb before his death, as part of the building works in Halicarnassus, so that when he died, Artemisia continued the building project. However, Artemisia spared no expense in building the tomb. She sent messengers to Greece to find the most talented artists of the time. These included Scopas, the man who had supervised the rebuilding of the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus.
I doubt i'll travel so far into the east, you'll better ask someone else.
If you change your mind, you know where to find me!
Thank you again! Your name will most certainly be accredited to in my next published work.

Have you explored all the seven Wonders?
Please return to me once you have! I'm eager to read your account!

It's good to see you again! Did you have a chance to visit all of the Wonders during your long journey?
Yes, Philo, i've explored all of them, here's my account!

Thank you, my friend! It is quite the undertaking to gaze upon all the seven great Wonders in one lifetime, this I know, and thus I sought to bring them to the common populace of all the world, by virtue of a written description of each. By reading of each of these wonders, one digests their majesty in a different way; their mind is etched with the visage of these structures for all time, unlike simply gazing upon them once, for after they leave, this image will be forgotten, purged from memory in place of memories anew. Unburdened by the weight of travel, my book finds its purpose. Please accept this gold as your payment! It's Well deserved!
Greetings, Traveller! Are you one of those 'adventurers', searching for the Sword of Mars too?
What's this about? What exactly is the Sword of Mars?

So you haven't heard? A few days ago, a group of men visited this tavern, apparently they have found a clue about the location of the legendary Sword of Mars! It's an ancient legend about a divine weapon wielded by the Scythian kings. It is said that whoever carried it, through the sword of Mars supremacy in all wars was assured to him!
Do you know where these 'adventurers' were heading?

They've learned that the relic was buried with the last of the Scythian Kings, Kanites. Few know that those large mounds you see throughout the steppe, are actually ancient burial sites, but nobody knows where exactly King Kanites was buried. The adventurers apparently visited some mounds, but found nothing, and as far as I know, they were planning to travel westward...
Aye, i'd like to search for the Sword too! What's it to you?

Thats a grand undertaking, were I younger myself, I'd join on your adventure! But someone like you will not be able to utilize such a magical artifact. If you find it, bring it back to me and I'll reveal it's secrets!
You carry the Sword of Mars, you're destined for greatness!
'The Sword of Mars' Part 1: Legacy of Scythia
According to the legend, the Sword of Mars must be buried with the last king of the Scythians. I must explore ancient burial sites on the steppes to find the ancient blade.
'The Sword of Mars' Part 2: The Rusty Blade

The old sword's golden scabbard and handle is remarkably well preserved, but the iron blade is completely corroded. Oricos offered to forge a new blade for the sword, but he requires 5 Iron Ore to begin the work.
'The Sword of Mars' Part 3: Payment in Blood
As payment for the repairs, Oricos asked me to track down and defeat a party of Itimarians, steppe nomads from the north of the Tanais River, who had been raiding his caravans.
'The Sword of Mars' Part 4: Thief in the Night

While i was in the north fighting, somebody broke into Oricos' workshop and stole the Sword of Mars! They must have taken it to one of their nearby hideouts! I must search 3 of these Steppe Bandit hideouts and return to Oricos.
'The Sword of Mars' Part 5: Prisoners of Woe
After an unsuccessful search, Oricos suggested a different approach; I must take a few steppe reavers prisoner for interrogation. One of them ought to know the man who stole the sword!
'The Sword of Mars' Part 6: The Duel
Spakos...The man who dishonorably took the Sword of Mars from me. I must confront him in the arena and show everyone that I am worthy to claim it!

Is that...The Sword of Mars? It's unbelievable! Long centuries have passed since this blade last tasted blood, you'll need a blacksmith to restore the sword to it's original glory! Fortunately for you, I'm the best blacksmith around!
Yes, but the blade is completely rusted... can you repair it?
You can forget the blade, I'll have to make a new one... However my latest shipment of smithing supplies never arrived, you'll have to provide that yourself; 5 pieces of Iron Ore should be enough.
Hello again! Do you have that iron for me?
Yes, here it is! Now tell me, how much would it cost me to forge the new blade?

I have something better in mind: Itimarian raiders have been looting my shipments for months. Let's say, you defeat one of their warbands and I'll repair the sword for you! This way you have the opportunity to show you're a capable fighter, worthy of the blade!
I have terrible news! The Sword is gone! The night after i finished assembling the reforged weapon, somebody broke into my workshop and stole it!
What!? How could that happen? Nobody knew that you had it...right?

Well, i may have told some people...But who could keep something like this a secret? It's the finest work I've ever done! Anyway, I have a trusted source who says the thief was the local 'representative' of a bandit gang that roams these steppes, he must have taken it to one of their hideouts!
Welcome back! I take your search was unsuccessful?
Sadly, yes. Do you have any ideas where to search next?

No, but perhaps there is someone else who might... if you could capture a few of the steppe bandit leaders alive, they might reveal the identity of this mysterious thief! Half a dozen of them ought to have one with the information we need...

You've returned with some prisoners! I heard one of them already spoke of a name...Spakos. I know that man, he is one of the local arena champions! Spakos is an experienced warrior, and if he possesses the Sword of Mars, there's no telling what he's capable of!
No matter. I shall kill him and take back what's mine!

Yes, but remember; The Sword of Mars is a weapon of spiritual power, you must win it back in a fair fight! If you do, people will see that you're truly worthy of it's power! You must confront Spakos in the arena, in front of everyone to see!
I'm sure you still have things to do...
What a fight that was! You're a true spiritual successor of the ancient Scythian Kings!
Thank you Oricos, with this blade, i'll bring glorious conquest to those who stand in my way!
And I wish you good luck in the wars to come! Here, take the Sword of Mars and a small purse of gold for the trouble I've caused. Goodbye friend!
Thank you Oricos, with this blade, i'll achieve peace through strength and bring justice to those like Spakos!
And I wish you good luck in the wars to come! Here, take the Sword of Mars and a small purse of gold for the trouble I've caused. Goodbye friend!
Good day to you, Stranger! Do you happen to be that mercenary I keep hearing about?
Possibly...Do you need help with something?

That's right. I have a little problem with rebelling farmers, slaves and brigands in Gallia. They call themselves the 'Bagaudae', freedom fighters against tyranny. What a load of manure! These bands do nothing more than terrorize honest folk and pillage the countryside. They must be dealt with...
So you want me to hunt down this rabble?

Yes, if you're up to the task. These brigands tend to form large raiding parties, nearing the size of armies, but of course they lack weapons and discipline, so they would pose little threat to an experienced commander.
Alright, I'll deal with these Bagaudae. What can you offer in return?
You'll have to clear out the countryside, which means at least 10 raiding parties. I can pay 500 coins for each, and I'll give you an excellent piece of armor as a reward!
Where can I find these bands?
They dwell mostly to the north of here, you'll find these wretches all over Gallia. Believe me, it won't take long until you run into some of them...
Why did the Bagaudae rebel against Rome?
You know how it is; the common folk always complain about taxation, corruption and wealthy landowners. Of course there is truth to that, but that doesn't excuse banditry and murder.
No, thank you, I'm not interested.
No, you're confusing me with someone.
The roads of Gallia are much safer thanks to you.
Return to Ausonius in Burdigala and let him know that the Bagaudae are dealt with.
Have you dealt with those brigands yet?
There are some smaller settlements they like to use as their base of operation. Keep your eyes open!
I've heard you've been busy on the roads. Are the Bagaudae dealt with?
Ten parties down. But I have a feeling this will not silence them for long...

True, there will always be those desperate enough to turn to open rebellion, but for the time being, the roads are safe, and Gallia can breath again! Thank you for your service, here's your well deserved reward!
Good day to you! You're not from around here, are you?
No, i've just arrived. Why do you ask?
That's good! Perhaps you could help me with something, but you must keep this a secret!
Tell me more about this problem, and I'll see if I can be of service.

Of course. Here's the situation; Agents of the Arcani have infiltrated Londinium. They have killed one of my informants and tried to bribe the other. I don't know who I can trust anymore. I had thought that we overcame the Great Conspiracy, but it's roots run deeper than I ever imagined...
Agents in Londinium working against Roman interests? Is there anything we can do?

We must draw them out of the shadows. I know they want me dead for my role in their persecution, so I will spread the word that I'm spending some time on my estate near Moridunum, alone, and far from the city guard. If I'm right, they'll be waiting for me there in ambush.
That's a good plan. Not without risk, but I can handle it!

You're right, there are no guarantees when it comes to dealing with the Arcani. They are very experienced fighters and masters of ambush, but above all, they are corrupt to the core. Be cautious, and trust no one!
This sounds too risky for me.

Not too long ago, there was a coordinated attack on Britannia. Picts from the north, Hibernians from the west and Saxons from the east, but the worst of all, it turned out to be planned by some of our own officials, like that accursed Valentinus, who bribed our garrisons and corrupted the Arcani. After a year long campaign, we pushed back the invaders and rounded up the traitors, but at a great cost.
And who are the Arcani exactly?

The Arcani were an ancient organisation, a specialized military reconnaissance force, who protected Britannia for centuries. Their official duty was to serve as couriers and intelligence gatherers for our generals, seeking information about disturbances among neighbouring nations. But in the decades preceding the conspiracy, they became corrupted, bribed with great sums of plunder, or at least, promises of it, to reveal to the enemy from time to time what was happening on our side. The most faithful agents of Rome turned into the greatest asset of the enemy...
This sounds too risky for me.
Very well. But speak of this to no one.
My name is Civilis, i serve as Vicarius of Britannia.
No, i don't want to be involved.
The Arcani pose no threat anymore, thanks to you.
Find the Arcani near the village of Moridunum.
Return to Civilis in Londinium and let him know the Arcani have been dealt with.
How is our plan coming along?
You mustn't tarry, it's just a matter of time until they learn of our trap!
Wait a minute, you're not Civilis! What's your business here?
He sent me in his place, and good warriors with me. Your little conspiracy is over, prepare to die!
That's the last mistake you'll ever make. Arcani, Strike!
He sent me in his place, and good warriors with me. But there's no need for bloodshed, I can pay 1000 gold to disband your company!
Thank you for your gold, your generosity will be remembered! However, I cannot allow you to walk away from this encounter alive. Arcani, Strike!
I'm so glad you've returned, i was worried to death!
Naturally. If they had killed me, you'd be next. But I'm alive and the Arcani have been dealt with.
Thank you so much! You've done a great service, not just for me, but for Rome itself! Here's your reward.
Welcome! May the Gods watch over you!
My name is Rufius Caeionius Sabinus, priest of Jupiter and faithful follower of the old ways.

Indeed, I am! There are dark times ahead. There's a bad omen every single day, I can barely sleep at night. And now, I hear that the forge of Vulcan, Mount Aetna has erupted! Rome has drawn the ire of the Gods, for too many of us forsake them in favour of the 'One God'.
We live in dire times, of that there can be no doubt. But is there anything we can do to appease Vulcan, and calm his forge?

We must do what can be done, even if it's not much. The restoration of our traditions starts with you, my friend! To regain the favor of the Gods, you must travel to Mount Aetna and seek the shrine of Vulcan, the god of fire! A grand offering should calm his temper. If you visit the mountain, please report the magnitude of the devastation! Here, take this gold for your journey.
Your superstitions are a relic of the past, I'll have nothing to do with it!
I'm sorry, I have to be on my way...
Mount Aetna's fires are still burning, we can only hope Vulcan's wrath will diminish in time.
Travel to the Mount Aetna and honor the Shrine of Vulcan. (Optional: Visit at night)
Report back to the Rufius Caeionius Sabinus
Return to Rome and tell Rufius Caeionius Sabinus about your journey to Mount Aetna.
Have you visited Vulcan's shrine yet?
Make haste then! Vulcan's wrath grows every day.
You've been to Vulcan's Shrine then? What did you see?
I have. Mount Aetna is engulfed in smoke and there's a river of fire flowing down it's slopes. The area is devastated and there's little sign of life...
Gods, have mercy on us! Thank you for honoring Vulcan in such a dangerous time, now, we can only pray that the forge of the Gods will settle once more. Here's the payment I've promised you.

The Bucellarii, meaning 'Biscuit Eaters', are groups of escort troops used in the Roman Empire, employed by high-ranking military figures or civil office-holders.
The Symmakhoi, meaning 'Allies', are groups of foreign mercenaries, serving in the Eastern Roman Empire.
The Unnigarde are a unit of Foederati in Roman service.
I was a smith. As you can see I'm a big fellow, strong... I was good at my job. Had a nice shop on the high street through my town. Saved a bit of money and thought about finding a girl to wed.
Yes. Too many men on both sides of the law prey on the weak.

Well, now there's a war on, and few are bothering with racing chariots. I went to find work with the armies. At first they had me fixing carts, but it turns out my skill with wheels came useful in making a catapult torsion twist. So I learned a bit about that. A lot about that, actually.
Wait... This famous stand you're describing. It was against your own side?

As it happened, my neighbors needed to supply an armed man for the king's levy. None of them wished to go, so I offered to stand in for them. They bought me a sword, jerkin and horse, and thus I became a warrior.

Maybe they were like that once, but they'd changed. They robbed, forced people to give them food, called poor farmers 'spies' and killed them just to strike fear in the others. So I said one day, 'You're all a bunch of common bandits.' They came to kill me, my cousin stood up for me, and they knifed him.

I don't know what I thought would happen... A good clean fight? The leaders executed, the rest let go? No, they took all 20 of that gang, including some who were barely old enough to grow a beard, and left them hanging to die outside the castle. I'd see those bodies twisting and think, 'This is my work,' and that was something I want no part of.

But everyone else - they're beasts to him. And he's a beast to them. And maybe a day comes that he's gone too far, and the lord is wondering whether to hang him, and a word from you determines whether he lives or dies. And if he lives, that means more peasant women will be raped and old men cut open to look for jewels in their bellies.

I fought as best I could, but the imperial forces took me prisoner. When they found that there was no one to ransom me, they let me go on my pledge that I would pay them later. It was a most noble gesture of them. So, I feel that I have no choice but to earn the money.
Very nice. You sound destined for the scaffold, so you might as well enjoy a hot meal or two.

The lords and the merchants, they sit in their lofty towers making grand decisions, but they don't see into the back alleys to know what plots are going on. They don't know where to find the debtor who won't pay his debt. They don't know where to find the wagging tongues starting rumors. So that's where I come in.
I was a gamekeeper near here. For a lord whose name I will not mention. I was taught to track deer and boars. But my master wanted me to go after other game.
Sure, I'll tell you my tale. Don't expect a happy one.
Well, before we begin, here's a flagon of ale to your health - both physical and spiritual.
I fought with the Company of the Boar. I was an armorer, a smith. They're a hard lot, though. I think you'll find a lot of us who've left them and gone looking for other work.

My father had five sons. That wasn't unusual, but what was unusual is that we all made it to adulthood. There wasn't enough land for all of us, so the two youngest of us moved to Charas. Found work on the wharves, hauling in cargos from all the ships coming in. For a few years, it was good work.

My first foray into war, we were pursued by a force of imperial cavalry twice our number. One man was needed to stay behind and hold a ford, so that the rest could escape. The others had families, so I chose to be that one, as I could think of none who would mourn me.
Aye, well, that shows how far honest work gets you.
Mmm... I do appreciate virtue, but villainy makes for a much spicier tale.

Anyway, you hear of someone who might have work for me, you let me know.

I am sorry for your loss.

I am Ammianus Marcellinus. I have served under countless notable commanders. Emperors and those who report directly to the Emperor.

Apollonius. Comes limitis Aegypti - count of the Egyptian frontier. Born in the Taurus hills, in Isauria, where a rich man owns two goats. I came down out of those rocks with a spear and a bad accent, and I soldiered twenty years before they gave me a river to guard.

I am Conon, a Protector Domesticus, in service to the Praefectus Aegypti. You might have heard my name, for many speak of my achievements. But even among my peers, my name is known best as “Conon the Barbarian”, a name spoken with malice and ill intent, for my mother was not born of Roman stock.

I have won at the games in Antioch and served the Praefectus Maximus in Egypt with my brother Phanes. I also am a great Rhetor, or at least I think as much. The ancient cynics are my guide in thought and writing.
I served as tribunus over a numerus of the Auxilia Palatina in the Persian war, and then left for Ctesiphon as a diplomatic hostage.
I studied under Zeno of Cyprus at the school in Alexandria where I learned the medical sciences and then moved on to be the personal physician of the divine Julian himself.

I am Philo, of Byzantium, a learned man and author of “De septem orbis miraculis”, a novel whose purpose is singular; to bring the might and beauty of man’s greatest architectural achievements to all who read it.
I'm a physician, trained by the well respected master, Priscianus!
I'm a master of the Alchemical arts passed down to us by the angels who fell from Heaven and taught all the forbidden aspects of nature to women.
It's no exaggeration to call myself a master archer, the best in all of germania!
I'm Alruna, wife of Aigil the Marksman. He is in a different town running an errand.
I'm a berserker from Scandza, looking for adventures in these lands.
I'm Charietto, the headhunter. If you need somebody dead, you call me. I've been taking on many bounties for various warlords along the Rhenus river.

The Suiones are the greatest tribe of Scandza; the land beyond Germania, who have always been ruled by my great clan, the Ynglings. We are famed for our ships that are swifter then Thonar's Chariot, perfect for raiding poor fishermen. I was king of the Suiones for most of my young life and my brother Alaric ruled with me. But we were both in love with the same woman, a shieldmaden - a temptress, who played upon our jealousies!

I am Fraomar, once King to the Bucinobantes, and all of the Alemanni. The tale of how I reached such greatness is known by all in these lands. Our people were oft a thorn in Rome’s side, pricking their lands and bleeding their coffers dry with glorious war. King Macrian, whose name I loathe to speak, led us many times into the Roman lands, in search of plunder.
About eight years ago, i was involved in the battles of the Roman Emperor Valens, fighting against the usurper Procopius, far from home.
I'm Masila, from the Suebi tribe.
I've served under Emperor Valentinianus for a decade, until six summers ago. We were leading a punitive expedition against the alemannic petty king, Rando.
I'm Sela, pirate captain, at your service!

You may have heard of Sigurd the Dragon Slayer. A legendary warrior, strong enough to throw his opponents over the shieldwall. Yet although he posses brute strength, he fights with speed and grace, unlike most fighters.
The Amali have a long and proud history, intermarried among all the Gothic peoples and those we have subjected to our sway.

People talk too much, especially at taverns. And it is my job to listen. Most people tend to avoid me. It suits me well. Catch unwanted attention in my work and you end up dead, which makes blending in with the crowd the best option.

I grew up in Dacia and Gothia, but have already travelled far in my young age in the employ of the Romans. I have served in the retainers of many optimates, and was trained in the Roman manner in their employ.
I was one of his many pupils who helped translate the bible to Gothic, and created a new script for my people.
I was consecrated by the great father Eusebius of Nicomedia, pupil of the school of Lucian of Antioch and friend to Arius.
My name is Alpabay, son of the great King, Balamber!
Back in my day, when we lived far in the east, i was respected as a warrior and a leader.
I'm Eskam, Shaman of the Eternal Sky!
Not a flattering title, but i care not for flattery. I've been striking fear into my enemies hearts since i was boy, and as a warrior, fear is my greatest ally.

I've been living in the steppes all my life. After my parents died, i had to learn to survive by myself at an early age. I became a good rider and archer, and i can take care of myself in hand-to hand combat.

My name? Visvadeva. Born a noble tradesman, and an advisor to the Kushanshah, like my father, and his before him. I have been trading across these lands for the better part of 6 years. My work has taken me across the silk road several times, in service to the last great Kushanshah. I dealt in silks, of course, and all manner of fine wares the Far East can offer. *He pulls out a coin from a distant land, and gazes at it*
I'm Dula, some call me 'Prince Dula', although i'm related to royalty only by fellowship, rather than blood.
But all that doesn't matter anymore. I'm disgraced amongst my people, brought shame to my family name forever...

I'm a simple herdsman from a village near Gargaza. I've learned how to use the lance and ride a horse, but other than chasing away some raiders from the village, i've never really had the opportunity to try myself in real combat.

I was born high up, where a boy learns the mountain before he learns anything else. I was a guide before I was a soldier. Snow, passes, which slope holds your weight and which one comes down on top of you. That was everything I knew at fifteen, and it turned out to be enough.

Arash. Yes. That Arash. My father named me for the archer who shot the border of the world - one arrow, loosed from Damavand, and it drank his whole life on the way out. I grew up on the Oxus. They point across the water at a walnut tree and swear it's the one. For a coin they'll row you over and show you the hole.

My father rode with the Immortals. The real ones, the King of Kings' own ten thousand. He died out in Gandhara putting down a rebellion, and an elephant went over him. They told my mother his head burst like a lemon in a press. They told her that as a kindness, so she'd know it was quick.

Rost-Sohunum. The Romans couldn't get their mouths round it, so they called me Barsumas, and it stuck the way a bad name sticks. Before any of that I rode ahead of the King of Kings' columns. Water, ground, which roads take a wagon and which ones only look like they do. I could count a camp from a hillside and come back with the number right. That was all I was worth. It was enough.

Bineses. That name once opened gates in Ctesiphon. I rode with the King of Kings' horsemen, and at Nisibis a Roman arrow found my mount's throat instead of mine. They didn't finish me. They knew what a highborn Persian is worth by the pound.

I ride messages. Have done since I was thirteen. My father put me on the post roads because I was small and light and the horses lasted longer that way. Five years of it, and I know every well and every relay post between the mountains and the marshes, and not one person who matters knows my face.

Khorohbut, when I was born. In Armenia - which has been fought over so long that who owns it is a matter of opinion. I kept accounts for the King of Kings. Stores, remounts, salt and oil, what a province owes against what it actually pays. Twenty years of it. I have never held a sword, and I have starved more armies than most generals.

A noble of Persia, which is a thing you inherit and then spend your life explaining. Eleven years ago the King of Kings sent two men into a Roman camp to finish a war. The Surena was one. I was the other. Every account you'll ever hear gives the Surena's name. Not one of them troubled with mine.

A Syriac, born in Adiabene. That makes me the King of Kings' property and the Church's problem. My grandfather tended a sacred fire for forty years and died with a cross in his hand. Nobody in my family has been one thing for long. They taught me medicine first and scripture after, and I have had more use out of the medicine.

Mihr-Shapur, if you want it whole. Named for the god who keeps the sworn word. I grew up in Ctesiphon - not the part with the gardens. There was a Roxolani in the city watch who had me on a horse before I could reach the stirrups. Everyone knows the Parthian shot: turn, shoot over the tail, ride on. He taught me there is no behind. Any angle, at a gallop, and no turn to warn you. I can use a blade too. Nobody remembers the blade.
My name is Mikula, a simple peasant from a village you never heard of.
I've traveled the world for ten years now, from the frozen coast of the north, to the magnificent walls of Constantinopolis!
People call me Volkh, the Wolf-Man. As you can see, i have a wolf pelt on my shoulders, but i assure you, i'm no maneater!
My parents immigrated to the empire when i was little, and by the grace of the Emperor we've been given land.
We live in a period where a slave may become master, and his deeds can become mythical. Those that exist simultaneous either follow, confront, or observe. I am the latter, but which are you?
In an effort to chart the outbreak of plagues and maladies that afflict us, I have been pursuing inquiries as far south as Numidia.

In my time spent here, many travelers come bearing trading goods and tales. We've seen men cut from multicolored cloth, telling stories of beasts, half-men, nymphs and battles. However, that does not concern me.
The pain that suffering incurs is no stranger to any living being. Just like you, I am more than familiar with suffering: I am comfortable around it, which allows me to work.
I've fought in countless arenas, particularly in the East. The din of the crowd and the faces of enemies are blinded by survival. I do recall fighting alongside -and against- my brother Horus.

I am a man of science. My primary science? Military science. My fascination with soldiery extends beyond simple plebeian adoration for procession, pomp, circumstance and the glory of conquest. War is itself a science that requires multiple ingredients to ensure maximum efficiency: training, organization, discipline, even the utilization of music is designed to keep the very soldiers in time! It seems ridiculous, but by God’s grace, it works!
My father was originally from the Spet Xyon tribe and my mother is the local governor's daughter.

But I am no longer. They rejected me, for my ideals, and cast me away. For the beliefs of my peoples were never shared in my heart. I felt no love from our gods. Instead, Allah found me, the God of the al-Rum, the Romans. For this, my punishment was exile.

I have been contracted into the service of many noble lords, for my skill as an architect is legend. There is a fine art in my work, I think. Few seem to accredit the great achievements of our forebears, their great towers and statues standing tall against the passage of time, to be gazed upon for millenia. Take the great dam of Ma’rib, its waters have fed the peoples there for a thousand years, if not more. One day I will leave my mark upon this world, my name unforgotten. *He turns the scripts in his hand to you- revealing a jumbled mess of lines* This, this will be my apotheosis. A grand palace, so incredible its majesty will herald the only finest of kings. Of course, you surely cannot see its beauty in these pages. You are but a layman in my craft.

I have only recently finished my studies, and hope now to seek a notable position in the local court. Although I bear little real experience in matters of state, and martial affairs, I am well versed in both law and scripture, with a wealth of knowledge of the histories and affairs of mine and other peoples.

I see now that our land is on the precipice of great change, where such small action could influence our history for years to come. I find myself thinking back to the grand and skillful leadership of the great Mushegh I Mamikonian, the great sparapet who stood against the vicious Sasanian monarch, Shapur II at the battle of Bagavan, where our people stood victorious. A man such as him could shift the winds of fate in a time like this, where our land is so fragile, being doggedly hacked at on all sides.

After the fateful treaty between Jovian and Shapur II was signed, our land's fate was damn near sealed. Conflict broke out with little delay, and we fought valiantly, those of us that did not see the fracturing land and sided with the Persian enemy. Many of my fellow nobles defected in this time, but I remained loyal. After a long and bloody conflict, Arsaces II held court with the Persians, and was captured, being taken to some unspeakable place. Our land was left leaderless. The one true heir, Pap, stayed with the royal treasure in the fortress of Artogerassa with the Queen mother Parandzem. Me and my brethren were prepared to defend this fortress to the last man.

A deep knowledge and love of our lord is paramount to living a rich life. In these trying times, where our people are fraught with challenges, with war raging across the world and our homeland being the battleground for great empires since time immemorial, spiritual guidance is greatly needed, and in short supply. With this, my job grows harder with every passing day.
But that's not all i am: i'm a warrior and leader of a band of fianna, some of them might even be around the town.

We gathered, forged an army and set out to combat the bastards. We met and fought bitterly, but my men were overwhelmed. The Picts took me prisoner and marched me back to my own home, forcing me to provide them with spoils. They sought to make an example of me before my kin, but my imprisoned kin were able to create a distraction to allow me to escape. Riches, furs, lands, women. All gone.

You'd like a history. Here's what's true instead. I know which wells are sweet and which are only patient. I know the name your mother nearly gave you. And I know what's under the barrow at the end of your road, which is why nobody ploughs it.

I was a grown man in the days of the Hound of Culann. I watched the Morrigan come low and black across a field once, and everything her shadow touched was dead inside the year. Then Rome came and drew a wall across the neck of this island. One people, cut in two, and the halves have been strangers ever since. I've seen that wall go up. I've seen it come down. I'm not finished watching it.
I've been teaching the art of war for a decade, trained many well respected warriors, most of them are still alive thanks to my techiques.

The beast was ferocious, and after it noticed me within the fence, it charged me with deadly force. The only chance i had was to pick up a nearby stone and smash in it's head. After witnessing what i've done, Culann was impressed by my strength, but the loss of his dog devastated him.

A long time ago when i was a young lad, one day i walked through a forest when i heard the cry of a small babe, barely a day old. I took him home and raised him as my own. Only later did i discover who his mother was, the Queen of the Iverni!

The levy took both my brothers when I was fifteen. Sent over the sea to hold a river neither of them could name. Nothing came back - no word, no bones. And the tax fell the same that autumn, counted against the two of them as though they were still home eating. That's Rome. It takes your young men and your barley and calls it protection.

Seven years back the whole island came apart in a season. Picts down the spine of it, Gaels off the western water, Saxons in every river mouth on the east coast - all at once, as though they'd settled on a day. Rome had to send a man across the sea to hand us back our own province. I was thirteen, standing in a burnt yard, and I understood something the greybeards in that hall still won't: an empire that has to be fetched from overseas to save you has already gone. It simply hasn't finished leaving yet.

When the winds blew fiercest, and cursed be me, on the eve of the Shabbat, I knew that I had to draw the favour of our Lord. Thus I drew from my pocket the sacred Parashah, and let fly the rudder. The ire of the panicked passengers grew quickly, unsurprisingly. One foul-mouthed soldier of Arab descent drew his blade, threatening to relieve me of my head! But I kept to my reading. Only as the waves grew to wash the bile from all our stomachs, did I see that our lives were certain to be lost, should I not retake the helm.
I have served in the protectores domestici, guarding the Emperor, the court and the Empire. I can stem a charge from any man or beast.

That was nineteen years ago. The Blemmyes come, we chase them, they go, I write it down. I grew up swearing by the Thunderer on my mountain - now there's a cross over every doorway from the delta to Syene, and I could not tell you the year it changed. That is what this sun does. You look up and a life is gone.

Perhaps thanks to this, I am oft chosen for the most dangerous assignments, tracking Garamantian raiding parties and felling as many as I can. Give me a sturdy blade and a few good men, and I will inflict great pain upon the foes of Rome. As one strays further from the life-giving oases, the bitter sting of the desert sand drives the hardiest of men to madness and unquenchable thirst. This is where I do my best work. My tasks always send me deep into the rolling dunes and far beyond Roman borders, where our foes take refuge.

Naturally you may be more interested in my skills as a champion. I am a boxer, wrestler, and master of the schools of Pale, Pygmakhia, and Pankration. This has made me both a renowned showman and a valued member of Maximus’ retinue.
I have a great deal of experience both in the command of infantry and diplomacy, having fought in many battles under the Emperor Julian.
I was banished after I failed to save Julian from his mortal wound, and have served at foreign courts since, but have returned to Constantinople at Emperor Valens’ behest.

For it is quite the undertaking to gaze upon all the seven great Wonders in one lifetime, this I know, and thus I sought to bring them to the common populace of all the world, by virtue of a written description of each. By reading of each of these wonders, one digests their majesty in a different way; their mind is etched with the visage of these structures for all time, unlike simply gazing upon them once, for after they leave, this image will be forgotten, purged from memory in place of memories anew. Unburdened by the weight of travel, my book finds its purpose.
Together with two other women, Salvina and Leoparda, we've served in the court of the Western Emperor.
Alchemica is the study of the composition of waters, of growth, of movement, of embodying and disembodying, and drawing and bonding the spirits to the body.
One time a king heard of my talents and forced me to try to shoot an apple from my son's head. Proving myself is one thing, but to risk my child's life for it?
A few years ago, we together defended a keep by ourselves against a band of marauders.
For a while i was serving as chieftain for a king, fighting many battles and conquering lands, until no opponent remained worthy of my attention.

On one occasion, even the roman emperor hired me against a group of particularly troublesome band of quadians. Me and my merry men exterminated nearly all of the enemy raiders, taking the rest captives.

My brother and I quarreled. I had drunk too much. He slapped me with a loaf of rye bread, and I spit him upon my sword... My own brother! My sword-arm was stained with the blood of my kin! Oh the blunder, I fear the scalds may sing of Eric the kin-slayer for millennia. The sons of Alaric, who now rule the tribe, soon banished me for the murder

In the winter’s cold our thunderous march would sound, the belt and buckle of the icy Rhine felt by all, for miles across. Our swords fell upon the Roman garrisons like butchers to cattle, and their prized standards would be our treasure. On our second crossing two years hence, we found Rome and all her shields stood against us. At Solicinium, the emperor Valentinian I brought our beleaguered army to heel, and accords of peace were reached, with Macrian imprisoned, and myself to be put in his place.

After the battle of Thyatira, i made a decision that haunts me to this day. You see I was loyal to Procopius before realising that it was a lost cause, so I defected to Valens. I only betrayed Procopius out of survival, but he glared at me, his former friend, until his head was cut off in front of a cackling Valens. I still see the blood gushing out of the true emperor's neck, staining the turf red, as well as my hands

I've grown up in a farmstead near Eburodonum. My family isn't of noble birth, although we were often invited to the halls of Medoslanium, for my father was a literate man who served as scribe of the chieftain.

That dog massacred the entire town of Mogontiacum, and retreated to alemannic lands. Valentinianus was ruthlessly pursuing the enemy deep into their home territory. If you remember the story of the Teutoburg defeat, you might already know what a horrible idea that is.

Few people around here know that i was born a princess in a small kingdom in the north, but don't worry, i won't demand to be addressed as 'royalty'. Politics is boring and i hate my brother who's about to inherit the throne anyway, so i've decided to make a name for myself.

Well, that man is me. The admirers and poets tend to exaggerate things, painting me as some sort of legend. In truth, most of it comes down to a good fitness regime and a sharp mind. I train, I study, and I win.

While there are those who would say I come from a lesser lineage among my kin, my family has no lack of prestige or holdings. My canton is large with many warriors, and I have fought in many battles against the fair-haired horse-dwellers who encroach on our homes.

I usually don't open up to people like this, but you seem like someone who could make use of my services. You see, I deal in information. Local lords, crime bosses, merchants - they are all my clients. I know what goes on in town, the best deals at the market, and who goes in and out.

I am skilled in the use of the spear, sword, javelin, and shield, and also have basic training for fighting on horseback. With my skill and training, along with my growing reputation and connections with esteemed men, I hope to obtain command of my own numerus or be granted a canton soon.

Like my tutor, I am an advocate of the Homoian belief of the substance and nature of Christ, following in the footsteps of his master Eusebius. Unlike Arius, we believe Christ was not created out of nothing, but of similar substance as God from God.

I have travelled far and wide spreading the teachings of Arius and Eusebius across the Roman Empire and Barbaricum. Now I am leader and chorepiscopus of the Goths in Nicopolis, welcomed as a refugee of persecution by the late Constantius, and respected among the Christians of the empire.

You might ask, why am i holed up in a tavern, instead of the royal court in Atil? You see, my mother's relationship with Balamber wasn't exactly official, so the so-called 'nobles' call me illegitimate heir, even though i'm the oldest son of the king.

When we started the western conquest, enemies fell before us and there was more gold and silver than we've ever dreamed possible. But for me, the thrill of the hunt and the glory of triumph was itself the reward.

If you are not familiar with hunnic customs, know that shamans are the most important members of the tribe, right after the chieftains. We act as mediators between the spirit realms, scryers of the future and healers of both mind and body.
I've lived a life of raiding and conquering, always fighting in the first wave. I've learned that to ensure victory, it's best to break your enemies before the battle even starts.
For a while i've joined up with a group of bandits, but since a disagreement with the boss resulted in the loss of his head, my former associates have been hunting me.

I have watched my home nation crumble against the ebb and flow of the many invaders who covet our wealth, and now what remains of our land has been brought to heel by the Kidarite Huns. Our people were once the bridge between the east and the west, and now, look at us. Just another fallen kingdom brought into the cold embrace of our Sassanian overlords. Gold, you see, is my passion. Wealth beyond all measure is no easy thing to acquire, and I sought to bear as much as one can in a lifetime. But fret not now, stranger, I will not claw at your purse. Such things are a heavy burden to bear alone. One who carries great wealth must defend it, as I’m certain you well know. I have found myself at the wrong end of a sword too many times. *He opens his hand to reveal a scar across his palm* and recently, my string of luck has been cut short rather abruptly. You wish to hear this tale? Of course you do.
You see, i've served my time in the alanian army, and in one battle i was lucky enough to save King Beler after he got separated and dragged off his horse by bosporan infantry.

What happened? I'll tell you: Love happened. I've fallen in love with the wrong woman, none other than my wife's sister. After the husband found out about our affair, he challenged me to a duel to the death to defend his honor.

Life was hard, but i could always rely on my trusty steed, 'Kolos'. She was the best horse i've ever ridden, instictively knowing every command before even i would give the signal. I was planning to join the army as a lancer, to push back the invading huns.

Two winters ago a column got cut off in the high country. The officers went first, the way they do. Thirty-one men left and not one of them knew the passes, so they all turned and looked at me, and I started telling them what to do. Nineteen came down alive. I still know the other twelve by name. That isn't modesty. I just haven't worked out how to stop.

When I was seventeen the Chionites crossed the river at night. I loosed once into the black, at a range no man makes. In the morning their captain lay face-down on the sand with my arrow in his throat, and forty men had watched me shoot. They knelt. I never told them I could not see him. I have tried that shot every day since and never come close.

I mean to wear that armour, and then I mean to command men who wear it, which he never did. But I'm eighteen, and eighteen buys nothing here. I've stood in front of every hall between the rivers and been told to come back when I've a beard. Nobody takes you on until you've done something worth telling, and nobody lets you near a thing worth telling until somebody's taken you on. Try getting out of that.

The Romans took me alive in the second month of their invasion and kept me with the column. So I watched an army eat itself from the inside. They burned their own boats. Then they turned north, into ground Shapur had already stripped bare, and there was nothing out there. No forage. No water a man could keep down. They lay down in the road. Nobody made them. They just stopped. By the time their emperor was killed, that army was already dead. It just hadn't been told.

Rome and Persia made peace that spring. Captives went back across the river, name for name - mine was on neither list. Nine years I watched the seasons cross a window slit. I came home to another man's seal on my fields, and my own kin speaking of me like the dead.

Last spring I brought a sealed letter to a garrison and sat in the corner while the commander read it. Watched him go grey. Then watched him stand up and tell four hundred men something else entirely, and watched them cheer him for it. I rode out at dawn with his reply in my shirt. I've not been able to look at a commander the same way since.

Then Julian came down the Euphrates and I was taken with the baggage. They kept me eleven years and never once locked a door. I learned Greek because I was bored. I wrote down what Shapur did and what Julian did, both, exactly as it happened. Somewhere in all that I took the water and a new name, which was quieter than arguing about it.

Their emperor was three days dead and they had nothing left to eat. I could see that much in the faces of the guards outside. So I talked. Slowly. I asked after their health. I raised small objections and let myself be argued out of them. Four days I kept that conversation breathing, and at the end of it a Roman emperor signed away Nisibis - a city Rome had held through three sieges and never once lost - for the price of a road home.

I went west once, as far as Antioch. Three men there call themselves its bishop. Their congregations meet in the street and break each other's heads over which one is right. I came home and found Shapur's officers hanging my people for refusing the fire. I have sewn up both. You cannot tell the wounds apart.

Two years back a marzban's son went into a canal with three men on top of him. I put two arrows in from sixty paces in bad light and dragged him out. He lived. The reward went to the officer who reached us at dawn - his grandfather has a name, mine sells horses. That hour taught me more than six years of drill.
Although, i feel that i'm destined for something more. Growing up i was always the strongest amongst boys my age, first at fieldwork and my woodwork is still the best in quality.
I've witnessed things, you could never dream of. And i've written songs to pass on these magnificent tales for the generations to come!
During my years of adventuring, i made a name for myself as a capable mercenary and headhunter.
They have raised me to be a faithful servant of the Empire, so i've decided to join the army.
What matters is that you and I are creating history. Whether by swinging the sword or by scribbling with ink, we leave our mark on the world.

We have faced countless illnesses throughout the Empire's history, be it smallpox, malaria or typhoid. Just like a soldier, we must know the enemy, their movements and how to counteract them to preserve ourselves.
My thoughts are of Pilgrims. Men who've journeyed to the East to see where Christ walked. They follow His footsteps, heed His word, and give praise. I care not for fighting, but for illumination.
Do you think that soldiers are the only ones that bleed? I have delivered countless babes, nursed ailing wives and dispensed aid to ease their pain.
We have trained since childhood to become the best athletes, wrestlers and fighters. And our training payed out too: ten years ago we competed in the games in Antiochia and won our first victories!

You see, I have worked with comitatenses, the Palantini, Scholae and Limitanei. I will not bore you with their names. I have seen the execution of their will on soldiers throughout the Empire: against barbarians and Eastern interlopers.
Growing up, they've always told me that one day i can take my grandfather's place and rule the city. I've learned four languages, trading and the complexities of city management.

Since then, I have ventured between the deserts and oases I call home, seeking people of like mind, to share our stories and record the histories of the many tribes that call this region home. I think one day I will journey out from this land and share the tales of my people with the greater world.

I would hope only that the man who employs me in building such a fine structure should compensate me adequately. I must profess, though, I fear my work lacks a certain substance you see, for I have long hoped to gaze upon the great wonders of the west, I wonder if they can compare to the Great Arch at Ctesiphon, its grandeur ever standing over the cradle of civilization. Perhaps you require the aid of a masterful architect in your employ? I am acutely familiar with the construction of siege equipment and military engineering. My services would be of great value to you, and I would gain the chance to look upon the wonders of our world. For a fair price, of course.

'To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding.' My father read to me the parables of Solomon often. With wisdom, we fathom the nature of things, and make good choices upon them. With instruction, we teach by correction, warning, and discipline. And with understanding, we learn to apply what we understand to discern what is good and evil, what is truth and lie. These are the words one must remember in matters of justice, and good conduct in life.

With Rome to the west, and Persia to the east, our homeland makes the battleground for those two great empires. Surely the victor of one such conflict would find no great difficulty in dominating our quaint, but proud, land. Fellow authors such as myself find themselves in a time where history is ripe to be recorded in great detail. I hope only that I would be afforded the opportunity to see first-hand the inevitable conflicts which would surely decide the fate of our fragile kingdom.

But when we saw that those who led our invaders were none other than fellow azat noblemen turned traitors, our spirits wavered. The Queen, in her great wisdom, appealed to them, and speaking the name of her husband, the traitors joined our cause, and aided us in hatching an escape plot, to take the last of our royals to Marcianopolis. Our efforts were successful, although in the strife, our Queen fell. Now our land flourishes once more, with the reinstatement of a Roman-backed Arsacid king on the throne, we are in good hands. Now I have found time to raise my son Mesrop, who has now finished his studies, and hopes to follow in my footsteps as a servant of the Armenian people. Perhaps you've met him?

I hope that I might travel to the further reaches of our kingdom to aid those struck ill in battle, and ensure their safe passage to the kingdom of God. My teacher, the late Archbishop of Mtskheta, Jacob, taught me of the parables of Solomon: “the blessing of God is over the head of a just man; but wickedness covereth the mouth of wicked men.” I see now such wicked men surround our land, the evils of the Sasanian lords, and the fiery greed of the Eastern Romans. Such men will be the undoing of us, those who are righteous.
I could list the fulfilled prophecies and heroic deeds of mine, but the sun might set before i would finish it!
Days and days, I trundled and scavenged throughout until I came to the wall and plead my case. Now I brood as I wait for financial backing in order to muster an army and take back my home.

Water goes where it likes and takes its time about it. I follow it. It's running toward whatever you're walking into - that's the whole of why I'm sat here. Don't make an omen of it. Or do. It's an evening's entertainment either way.

Rome's turn is coming, mind. I've stood where the veil runs thin and looked through. Something is waking in the east. I saw the horse first - a dark one, shabby and low, with red eyes - and behind it the sky went black and buzzed with arrows. I don't know his name. I don't know whether he's one man or a hundred thousand. But the Morrigan kneels at the ford and washes the harness of the man who is going to die, and she is kneeling now, and the gear in her hands is Roman. The ones drinking tonight will die in their beds. Their grandsons will not.
Currently i don't have any new students, so if you wish to hone your skills with the sword, spear or javelin, you've come to the right person!

Something had to be done to rectify his loss. I've felt so guilty after killing my host's watchdog, that i promised to find him a new pup and guard the estate myself, until the dog is old enough to do the job. So that's how i became 'Culann's Hound'.

Niall grew up to be a capable man, after finding out about his royal heritage, he determined to reclaim his place in the royal court. And after years of struggle, he achieved his dream, now ruling as High King!

This island comes back to us one day, and not by asking. That day wants a man who can hold four hundred frightened men in a line. I can hold twelve. Doesn't have to be me standing there - it has to be somebody, and nobody's learning. So I'll follow someone who knows how, and pay attention.

When the legions go, this island will want one man over it, and I intend that to be me. But my people don't follow gold. They follow whoever they believe can't be beaten. So I'm out here collecting coin, and a reputation, and a name that walks into a room ahead of me. How I come by any of it is my own affair.

My wisdom saw us back to safer waters, for a time, only to see the stormfront tear our one sail down and leave us aground on a reef, stranding us in the middle of nowhere. Only with the guidance of a mal’ahkim, an angel of a man, did we finally find a safe port in Azarium. And now, relinquished of my coin and a debtor to many, I find myself in need of work.

This is my life. It is an honour that will be apprecaited. Simply mention my name at court, and you will see ears prick up and eyes dart in your direction. I contributed my sword arm, my attention to details, my tactical prowess, and my efficient management.
So I am leaving. Nobody has relieved me. I am simply going, and they can find the belt on a chair. Find me a war. I don't much care whose.

Even in my many victories, I feel the growing ire of my peers, their resent for me ever apparent. It seems even with an endless list of successful missions, the impurity of my blood cannot be forgotten. A shame, for I had long hoped to look upon the Great Palace at Constantinople, but I would never be stationed there, in light of my heritage. Now, perhaps you are in need of a fierce warrior, of battle-born stock, one who would see the heads off any of your opposition. In exchange, I would ask only that you bring me to the capital, to finally gaze upon the pinnacle of Roman civilisation.
Of course I can be discreet, although my fame can make it difficult. But an inconspicuous boxer and wrestler makes for a fine bodyguard that can blend in with the bureaucrats.
My time with Persia spared me the political backlash of his death, where many of my friends and colleagues were slain.
Now I am compiling a collection of all the great medical writers of ages past, like Galen and Heraklas, which I hope will become a standard among my colleagues.

Truly, the immeasurable majesty and splendour poured into these works beckons men to think of things far greater than themselves, and wonder at the very gods, who bless these works which honour them. Yet in all the majesty of man’s finest achievements, I cannot help but wonder will we ever, in our future, build anything as wondrous as the Hanging gardens, or the Great Pyramids. To see such works in their infancy would perhaps be the finest gift one such as myself could hope for. I can only pray that I am once more afforded the chance to travel the world, to look upon such great creations anew.

I remember the methods of Leoparda, by the Gods, they were awful! Even Priscianus noted in his book how her remedies are no more scientific than that of Dioscorides. I have no idea how she became a respected gynecologist...
I also study the transmutation of metals through purification. Much like a baptism, the divine water purifies the metal in the alchemical vessel with the tincturing vapors of mercury and sulfur.
I had no choice but to obey. But i readied two arrows: One for the apple, and one for the king, in case my first shot hit my son...
Of course being the master archer, Aigil dealt with most of the attackers, but those who made it close enough, met the end of my blade!
But i know little of Cimbria and the realms of the south. Tell me, are there worthy foes in these lands?
As it happens, the son of the quadian king was leading these raiders! Needless to say, the king pleaded for peace immediately, fearing for the life of his son. In other words, i ended a war!

I trekked south with only a sword and a slave, the latter coming in handy, sleeping in barns until I reached a great empire, with roads that I could travel on at double speed, leading to cities of stone and brick and winters mild. Being betrayed by my now distant tribe, I aspire to Romanitas, I even tried becoming a citizen a couple of summers ago, serving the auxiliary, before realizing that brigands would treat me better.

With this new standing among my people, and commanding a substantial force, I was tasked by my new Roman overlords to bring the devastated lands of Britain back into the fold. I appointed command of my forces between two trusted chieftains- Bitheridus, and Hortarius. My faith in the latter’s stock, however, was misplaced. Hortarius, all that time, conspired with Macrian to have me deposed! Having learnt of this treachery, I made certain his death was slow. It was clear then that I had no favour with my people, and I was pushed into exile; and Macrian reinstated, serving Rome as “foederati”, once again slaves to Roman wiles. Now, without a home to settle, my sword serves whomever carries the fattest purse.
My hands remains stained with the blood of Procopius, I cannot wipe off such a disgrace. After realizing what i've done, i've renounced my military titles and i'm living a simple life ever since.
I made plenty of friends with soldiers, often trained and hunted with them. Although i was never allowed to go on any campaigns yet, i think i am more than ready to become a warrior!

When we met the enemy, our chances were not much better, but with my disciplined men and competent leadership, we held the lines for hours. Finally, the alemannic ranks weakened and Sebastianus attacked them from the flank and routed them. By god, i have never seen so many dead bodies on a battlefield...

So that's why i'm here, gathering a group of brave men for my pirate brigade, to raid and plunder all the riches at the coasts if Scandza and beyond! You look capable, would you be interested in joining my band?

I've wandered the north, challenging the best warriors in each village to duels. These are times of war, however, and I have realized that maybe my talents would have more use in battle, leading warriors to victory.

I am travelling the world seeking allies in our fight against the Alans and these newcomers from the far East, a people that the Bactrian merchants call ounna. Many of the surrounding gentes have banded together against them, but raiding ravages our farms and hunger has set in, and my people grow desparate.

It's a lucrative business, but not exactly problem-free. With my kind of clients, it is inevitable to make some enemies along the way. In fact, and don't look now, I am quite sure that those men over there are ready to jump me as soon as I step out of the tavern.

I have made acquaintances in the highest echelons of the many Gothic courts and in the Roman military. However, I have been held back by my lack of lineage. The Romans have provided me my family and my education, but it has proven difficult to advance through merit in a court of intrigue.

My beliefs were condemned at Sirmium, but the imperial brothers’ wisdom has allowed me to again travel the world convincing others of Christ’s true nature. It is a dangerous life, as our Christian communities fight among each other instead of the unbelieving.

I have written many works on theology and exegesis, and debated at the Councils of both Sirmium and Constantinople. My great work is the translation of God’s word into the language of my people, with the help of my devoted colleagues and pupils of our church

The worst part is that my half brothers always looked at me with disdain, and their mother even convinced Balamber to exile me. So now, i'm living life as an outcast, with no status, no name and no clan to call my own.

As for the other nobles: they kept pickering for even more treasures, slaves and lands for themselves. After a while i grew tired of the greedy bastards, and decided to let my sons carry my legacy onwards.

Without our guidance, people are hopelessly lost in the material world, unaware of the many harmful spirits who may hinder one's life. Shamans are able to gaze into other realms of existence, obtaining knowledge ordinary humans can never dream of.

I often challenge the enemy leaders to single combat, proving how cowardly they are if they refuse, or how weak they are when i tear open their guts in front of the entire army. No matter how they choose, the enemy spirits are broken from the start!
Now i'm without money, friends and luck. I'd very much like to leave town for greener pastures, bandit life was never to my liking anyway...

Myself and a small band of hired freemen were only a short ways out of Gandhara, making for the Jin peoples. But as we descended into a valley, a log fell afoot of my horse. In that very moment, a great wave of bandit filth came pouring out of every bush and tree and we were quickly surrounded. Many of them, I felled with my bow, before I was forced to flee. The scum gave chase, and I was quickly brought to heel with an arrow in my precious mare’s side. Those bastards must have thought me dead, for they stripped everything from me, and left me to rot in the rain. Everything I had, all that I was, lay in that caravan. And there was nothing left of it. What those dogs could not carry they burned. And now, me, one of noble birth, whose family served the Kushanshah, confined now to the last of our lands! To see an empire fall is a grim affair indeed.

After the battle, Beler was so grateful for my help, he offered a position within his bodyguard unit. As years gone by, i became a trusted advisor and a good friend of his. Since we were quite inseparable, he jokingly referred to me as his adopted son, hence the nickname 'Prince Dula'.

As you can see, i'm still here. But killing him was the easy part: now my entire family has turned against me, i have no friends left and even my lover has shunned me for killing her husband. I have no place left on this earth...
Sadly, Kolos has passed away last month, her meat was her final gift to me. Now i'm a rider without a horse, with no money to buy a new one. The only animal i have left is a stubborn mule...

Since then men do what I say and never ask themselves why. It works. I've stopped pretending I don't like that it works. So I came down to find out how far it carries, because there's nothing left to lead up there but goats and eleven households.
So either the blood is real and it comes back to me, or I am a liar with a famous name and four years of luck behind me. I mean to know which. I won't learn it standing in that village.

So I'll go somewhere nobody's counting my years, and I'll do it there. I'm the best sword west of the Euphrates. I know exactly how that sounds coming out of a face like mine. Put me in front of somebody and I'll stop having to say it.

Afterwards I went looking for the book that explained it. There wasn't one, so I wrote it. Old wars. Old roads. Men who walked into the same country four hundred years apart and died the same way, and not one of them had read a line about the one before. I keep waiting to meet a commander who has. Maybe that's you. Probably not.

Our priests say a person's glory - khwarrah, the light Ohrmazd lends us - never dies. It only walks off, and waits like a dog where it was dropped. Mine is lying in Roman mud. Give me a war and a commander worth bleeding for, and I'll go get it back.

Nobody lowers their voice for the courier. I've been furniture in thirty camps and I've watched more battles from a hillside holding somebody's horse than most soldiers ever fight in. I'd like to be in one. That's the whole of it.

I can't go back. The book is in my own hand and it does not flatter the King of Kings. And I will never be Roman - they hear it the moment I open my mouth. So I sell the only thing I have left, which is arithmetic. I know what salt and oil and a sound mule cost in three empires, and I know what a prisoner is worth to the coin, because I brokered eleven years of them.

You'd think that would be enough for one life. But a man who takes a province without a battle is an embarrassment to everybody who has ever fought one. There's no seat for me at court and no soldier will drink with me. So I've come out where the story hasn't reached, to be useful to somebody who doesn't much care how a thing gets done.

Not one of them was still warm when I reached them. Not one. So I take what's left - the bones, the names, what was done and who stood by while it was done - and I set it down while the people who saw it are still breathing. I'm carrying it west. It is not work a man does alone in a country that would rather he stopped.

The guard at Ctesiphon takes noble houses only. I've watched them on the gate. Not one could hit a wall from a moving horse. They're slower than me and they'll die older and richer. So I'll make myself into something the court can't step over, and I'll do it out here, where nobody's grandfather is watching. Then I go home.
But still, peasant life never satisfied me...
If you wish, i can sing you you a song about my voyages of the western sea!
As it turns out, it's beneficial to let people spread rumours about your exploits, it makes you more of a legend than a person. And with notoriety comes higher pay!
There isn't a more noble cause than fighting for the ideals you believe in!

Pericles himself said, 'What you leave behind is not what is engraved in stone monuments, but what is woven into the lives of others.' This cannot be disputed, and I seek to leave a similar mark on the world.
I consider it more practical than virtuous. There are notable similarities between soldiery and medicine, particularly strategies. What's your own strategy, sir?
I yearn to go East to make my pilgrimage, but I have no money to pay for passage or protection. Will you have me?
I am the physician Leoparda. I have worked alongside the Emperor's own doctor. Simply ask Priscianus, when he can be pulled away from his scrolls.
I can still remember the cheers and adorations of the audience. Those were the days! Since then life has separated us, i wonder what's Horus up to these days...

The drills, tactics, and methods they have permitted me to see? *pats his manuscript and then taps his skull* I assure you that with my knowledge, your army will know no fear, will know success, and will know to obey.

But my grandfather died too soon, may his spirit rest in peace, and since i was still a young lad, King Kidara chose my uncle istead for the position. Now i'm stuck here, wondering what I'll do with my life...
Of course. Perhaps also, I could record your deeds, and document your travels, let your name not fade into the sands of time, to be forgotten.
Of course. I am a master in my craft, and you will have no regrets in enlisting my service.

Indeed, one such as you surely has a vast font of knowledge that could be imparted unto me. I would be indebted to you for such a service, but I fear I cannot just uproot my life here, I would require a stipend to settle my affairs.

Of course. Perhaps then you would do well to take me on, for I am not just a historian, but a studious and learned man who has seen the skill of the sparapets, and have become quite familiar with their tactical excellence.
Quite right. The blood of my King's foes has stained much of my life. Perhaps I should keep my spear-arm in good shape. I'd join your retinue, for a fee of course.
Of course, I can aid your men in their departing to our God’s kingdom, and heal those whose time is not yet done. The minds of your men would be stronger with God in their heart.
Certainly! I have decades of training and experience in warfare, ambush, herbal medicine and archery. I'd be a valuable member of any company.

That's right! I'm thinking of mercenary work, I am a capable swordsman, spearman and you would not want to be on the receiving end of my bow or javelin. I can also instill discipline and loyalty in men with little effort

Suit yourself either way. I go ahead, and I come back knowing what's over the hill and who thinks he owns it. I talk people past men who'd sooner open them. And when talk runs dry there are quieter arts. You won't ask about those, and I won't offer.

Take the counsel or leave it - they mostly leave it. But hear what walks with me: your sick would mend, where now they rot, and that puts more men back in a line than any recruiter you could hire. Your people would listen to me, and there'd come a day you resent it. And I'd tell you what this ground will feed, before you march onto it hungry.
This wouldn't be the first time i fought alongside men like you. My skills with the sword and spear are unparralelled, just don't expect me to be your army cook!
This would not be the first time a warchief asked me to serve him. Know that i'm no ordinary footman! I've trained with Scatha, if you know of her, i need not say more!

What i did, i did for the boy's well being. I never wanted riches or titles. I'm a poet by profession who's rather perform songs of old and drink some good mead with my friends. I may be old, but i'm still an adventurer in heart!

However you answer, the offer doesn't change: a dozen of your worst and a fortnight, and you'll want them back. Front rank, blade and shield - I've no patience for reach. And when I've missed the sense of an order, tell me why after. I'm not asking to be humoured. I'm asking to be taught.

Either answer is the right one - that's the trick of me. I'm good in a fight and better before one: give me a day to look at a field and I'll tell you where they'll break. And when a thing wants doing that you'd rather not be seen doing, there are men you send and ask nothing after. Every leader needs one. Most work it out too late.
As you wish. I am doubtless a masterful navigator, and my faith never steers me wrong. Should I be made your retainer, I will keep your ship steady.

I would be of use to any commander, not just for my knowledge but my sword arm. I'm still breathing, am I not? In addition, I have observed many viable tactics, efficient stewardship of an army, and have managed countless prisoners.

Take me or leave me on this stool - the sand doesn't care and neither do I, much. I know sieges, I know how an army starves, and I can tell which of your men will run before he knows it himself. If you ever do want me, wake me before the fighting. Not after.

As you command. Should you enlist me in your service, I would ask only that you deliver me a small sum, such that I might beg my leave from my commanders. For this, I would reward you handsomely with the heads of your enemies.

You will find no better fighter than myself, except maybe those who are skilled with the sword or spear. I’ve taken a great interest in Drama and Cynicism recently, but would be glad to contribute my talents to your retinue.
Right, my talents with the spear, sword, and shield are many. I commanded infantry, but did so from horseback with the other officers, so I am an experienced cavalryman as well.

Right, I’m currently in the middle of my writing, but experience in the field is always relevant to my work. I’ve also consulted with the Oracle at Delphi, if you require such divine guidance in the future.
Very well. Should I join you in your travels, your name will most certainly be accredited to in my next published work.

I've actually studied and performed experiments with my remedies to improve what i knew or abandon the ineffective techniques. While Leoparda relies on 'traditional' methods, i'm actually able to save lifes, instead of just giving some opium for the pain.

I have written many works on these topics, containing knowledge in the purification of metals, in the creation of elixirs, and the spirit. I can create for you all sorts of concoctions from healing remedies to liquid fire.
As you can see, i'm still alive, so i never needed the second arrow.
