Well, i'm not much of a warrior, but i can defend myself and i can use the sling quite well! But i have other skills as well, i'm good at trading, managing a camp and i know many healing herbs.
Hmm, you don't look very strong. But there aren't any better choices around here either... Let's just say, i'll consider it.
May it be luck or skill, but the fact is, whoever i set my target on, is a dead man. But ever since my service with the emperor, i didn't have the most well paying employers.
One day I may enter Woden's halls for my valor, but i haven't found a worthy cause to fight for yet.
Very well. In your service I can assure you- while your enemies draw breath- my blade will never dull.
You're probably right. Perhaps there is still chance for me afterall!

Well, as you know, my father was a scribe, he taught me how to read and write, and i've read a lot about warfare and leadership. But when it comes to fighting, i can hold my own, and i'm a quite decent archer!

Yes. But on that day, it was avoidable. Honestly it was a miracle that we even beat them at all. Even though i've recieved honors for my bravery, i would never take part in such a disaster ever again!

Well, with you on board, that would be two already! That's a start isn't it? Alright, i see you're not convinced. But i'm serious about the pirating business! Believe me, i can swing an axe, hold a shield and row a boat as well as any pirate you know!
Maybe. But i'm not only a good fighter, but i've proven to be more fit for leading than to follow others. I will not fight for an incompetent commander!

As a noble of my house I am skilled on horseback and command, with great prowess with the lance, bow, and sword. Although I have not spent my life on horseback and shooting like the nomads who beset us, you will find few that can match me as a cavalrymen, and none who have my connections among the families around the Euxine sea.
Ha! I'm sure I can manage them on my own. But maybe it is time for a career change; it seems like I have outstayed my welcome here.
I have served the Romans loyally for some time now, but I seek whatever opportunity that comes before me, be that on the battlefield or in the political arena.

Like Ulfilas I have spent many years helping the Goths of Moesia, seeing to their needs and curing them of their ailments. I also have been quite charismatic in my debates with the followers of Arius and the adherents to Nicaea.

While I cannot condone the sin of murder and fight alongside you, I have been an administrator of my people and our community for many years now. I am a charismatic man in both teaching and debate, and have befriended many in the Emperor’s and Patriarchs’ circles, despite our differences in the particulars of Christ’s nature.
You're right, stranger. I'm thinking about making a name for myself as a warrior, show the world what i'm capable of! I promise you, one day everybody will know my name!

I've only said that i've left the politics behind, not that i've abandoned either my family or the war itself! I will join a warband soon, and make my children rich with loot and proud by bravery in battle! And if i fall on the battlefield, then i'll finally rest with a smile on my face!

It's true, i am young, but i've learned the ways of the shaman since childhood. You see, my father is a respected shaman of my tribe and he taught me well. I know which herbs heal or harm, or even induce spiritual encounters. But father said that i'll need more worldly experience before i can take my place as shaman of the tribe. So here i am, looking to find a place where i can utilize my skills.

Only if the enemy champion is my equal, which has never happened before. My arms are strong, my lance is sturdy and my armor is impenetrable! If you doubt my words, challenge me to a fight, i promise, it will be the last decision you'll ever make!
I was considering to enlist in the mercenary band called the Unnigarde, but they've moved west already. Until i meet them again, i'll consider other options too.

Right. Perhaps you and I, we could enter business together? My wealth of experience, with your... skill... we could make a lot of money together. I was born to serve kings, but you will do. Need I say more?

Well, times have changed. I had my disagreements with the other nobles about strategic decisions regarding the war with the huns and the king has taken their side over mine. I've been dismissed from my position, but i feel that's probably a good thing. I have never feared death, but i have to take care of my two daughters now, and this way i don't have to leave them as orphans by dying in a pointless war...

I know, Stranger. After i drink myself under the table, i'll take my belongings and head to Roman lands. Maybe there i can start a new life. I've heard they don't care much for who you are, as long as you serve
Even so, what kind of commander would hire an Alanian warrior who can only ride a mule into battle? I'd be laughed at for even suggesting such an idea.

Your company, your choice. But if you take me: send me ahead and I'll tell you who's watching a valley before they know you've entered it. And give me your worst men, the ones who argue. Those are the ones I'm any use with. The good ones never needed anybody.

Believe me or don't - you'd not be the first either way. But if you take me on, one thing: don't tell your men the story. Let them hear it from someone else, and let them believe what they like. It works better that way. It always has.

Laugh if you like - they all start by laughing. Keep me mounted and you'll see: on a horse before I could walk, decent with a bow, better rider than archer if you want it honest. But the sword is what's worth paying for. Put me where it's thickest and don't send anyone to help. I've never needed helping and I don't plan on starting.

Two things, whatever you decide. Send a man out a day ahead of your column - me or anyone - and learn what the ground allows before you've chosen what you want. And when your scout tells you a position is bad, it's bad. Don't argue it. I've seen what it looks like when a commander argues.

As you like. Only know what you'd be taking or leaving: a man who has held a line while arrows came down like rain off a roof, and who knows the hour a wedge breaks - always sooner than the young think. Ohrmazd keep your road, whichever way it runs. And if I fall in your service, waste no hole on me. Leave me to the sun and the dogs.

Either way, you should know what you'd be passing up: further in a day than anyone you've got, on worse horses, and standing at the end of it. Ninety miles once, on a bad ankle and a stolen mare. Ask me about water or a ford in flood and I'll know it. Only don't send me out carrying another man's letter.

Decide as suits you. But before you march anywhere: have someone check your quartermaster's tallies against what's actually in the carts, and learn how many days you truly have, not how many he says. And never send a soldier to buy your provisions. They see armour coming and the price doubles before you dismount.

Decide as you please - most men decide against me, and the slower ones live to regret it. I can tell you what an enemy can still do, which is never what he claims he can. And there will be days when the cheap way through is a delay, a lie or a bought man, and on those days you'll want somebody beside you who doesn't flinch. That's what I'm for. You needn't like me.

Every company that fights needs someone to sew it back together - yours too, whether it's me or another. Keep a surgeon out of the front rank and he'll hand you back men you would otherwise have burned. And when a gate stays shut, let him talk before you knock. I've walked a cart of bones through six border posts and paid a toll at none.
Take me or don't. But if you do, put me on a horse with room to move and I'll empty a flank for you. One condition. Keep your silver - just see that the right people hear whose arrow it was.
Bah! I was never fond of the high-handed mandates of the fancy lords, otherwise i could keep serving the village chief. No, i need a job with some autonomy, where i can fulfill my potential!

You don't think music and songs are useful for a company of warriors? If that's not enough, i have other skills that may be of use: i speak many languages, i'm able strike the best deals when bargaining for supplies and i can guide an army through seemingly impassable terrain. Is that useful enough for you?

Don't insult me! I'm a honest adventurer who takes his commitments seriously. I'm not telling the common folk what rumours to propagate. And i hope you won't find me immodest when i say, my exploits are worthy to tell tales about!
I'm not a roman by birth, but a roman in spirit! I believe i can achieve greatness, not just for me, but for the Empire!

First of all, I can swing a sword as any soldier can. But I can record your deeds spread your story for posterity and renown. I am also a capable administrator, so I can be of assistance with maintaining your camp.

Think about it! When your men fall ill, how will you keep it from spreading to your entire company? How will you treat it? Herbal remedies are reactive,but you could save the supplies. A commander must be proactive instead of being reactive.

This is not the first time I've traveled with soldiers. I've followed camps through difficult terrain, cooked enough meals to feed a legion and learned to be handy with a javelin when marauders would attempt to raid us
As a physician, I know what herbal compounds counteract pain and can mend bones. What's more, my steady wits and hands will not be interrupted when removing arrows
Well, i'm an arena champion, but i'm eager try myself in real combat, as long as i'm able to train and practice for the upcoming games!
Right. I'm currently writing a comprehensive militari treatise called De re militari, but i have experience with mercenary work too.
You're right, i'm still young, i have all the time i need.
Right or wrong, I cannot blame you for your anger.

I served in the free companies. When I was young and foolish I loved it - the danger, the comraderie. But sometimes something you see turns your stomach. Something you saw a friend of yours do in a looted city. I will not speak of it. I need a new road to follow.
Ah... I suppose I can tell you.
The way I look at it, we all fulfil the will of the Heavens in our own way. So I do what I'm good at.

One night I was walking home with my brother when we ran into a group working for one boss they called Big Tuna. Told us our crew had killed one of theirs, and they were going to kill one of ours in return. Took my brother, wrapped a heavy chain around his legs, and threw him into the water. I don't know why they let me live.
A fitting reward for a man who defied the order that the Heavens instituted on earth for our own good.
My father was even a little prouder than most, I suppose. One day he was insulted by the lord's bailiff and he upped and left, moved us higher in the hills to be away from all other men.

But with the wars, and a lot of people losing their land, things changed on the docks. Too many hands, and not enough cargos. Gangs from the back alleys started getting involved. If you didn't hire their people, maybe your ship would go up in flames.
I commend your love for your fellow man.
I am Safiyya, once a poet and storyteller in the Quda’a confederation of tribes. Should you seek a silver-tongued scribe to tell of your great deeds, I will be here.
I am Senemar, master architect and designer of fine palaces. For a fair sum I can build you weapons that will topple the tallest of walls.

My name is Mesrop Mashtots, learned son of Vardan, and hopeful servant to my people. I hope to find experience in service to a capable general, to learn all that one can in the matters and affairs of martial excellence.

I am Pavstos Buzand, chronicler of the histories of Armenia, from the lives and rule of our royalty, to the affairs of our greatest generals. My knowledge of the tactical minds of bygone eras would surely prove invaluable in your journeys.

I am Vardan Mashtots, noble azat & fierce defender of the Arsacid dynasty, and proud father to my son, Mesrop. If you want a masterful soldier who does not quake in the heat of battle, I am yours, for a fee.

I am Svimeon, priest of Kartli. I have long studied the words of our Lord, and the practice of medicine and healing. I can ensure the proper treatment of you and your retinue, in matters both physical and spiritual.
I'm a Druid and Fennid mercenary. I've led a company of warriors myself until i met you.
I was once the king of the Damnonii, until the Picts taken over. Now i'm travelling the country, trying to gather money and supporters, so one day i may reclaim my lands!
Modron. I know paths, and I know people, and there's less difference between the two than you'd care for.
Myrddin. Born under Yr Wyddfa when Rome was still a rumour on the wind. I heal, I counsel, and I know what land will bear. The rest you'll hear from other people.
I'm a teacher of the art of war, but i also have experience fighting in armies.
I'm a warrior and former guard of Culann, the smith. I've trained with Scatha in the art of war.
I'm a poet, but most people know me for being the foster-father of king Niall.
Uthyr Ddraig Goch - my grandfather's name, not yet mine. Rome took my brothers and went on taxing us for them. I'm learning to lead, so that someone can.
Vortigern. Third son of a hill chief, which means I own a horse. Rome's grip on this island is a loan coming due, and I mean to be the answer to what comes after.
I am Amarantus, sailor, merchant, and faithful child of Yisrael. Should you spill your coffers my way, I’ll see that any voyage you undertake is uneventful, and your passage calm.
I'm a military veteran. I have served in the protectores domestici, guarding the Emperor, the court and the Empire. I can stem a charge from any man or beast.
Apollonius. Count of the Egyptian frontier, Isaurian by birth. Nineteen years in this sun and nothing to show for it but a belt. I'm leaving. Ask no more than that.

I am Conon, or as those whom I serve alongside call me, Conon the Barbarian. I am the sword of Rome in these parts, for my deeds are great in both number and renown. Enlist me, and the heads of your foes would roll in great number.
I'm an Olympic champion, me and my brother Phanes have won many honors in the games.
I'm a veteran from the wars of Julian against Persia.
I'm a physician of renowned quality, i once served Emperor Julian, but after failing to safe him from a mortal wound, i was banished.

I am Philo of Byzantium, author of “De septem orbis miraculis”, and a student of man’s finest architectural achievements. I have long hoped to see the world and its Wonders once more, and should you afford me such an opportunity, I would be eternally grateful.
I'm a physician, trained by the well respected master, Priscianus.
I'm an alchemist, i have written many works on these topics, containing knowledge in the purification of metals, in the creation of elixirs, and the spirit.
I'm a master archer, the best in all of germania!
I'm the wife of Aigil the Marksman. I'm a good steward, competent trader and healer.
I'm a headhunter, adept in scouting, tracking and ambuscade. I'm a good fighter, but i excel at javelin throwing.
I'm an exiled king from the Suiones tribe, from the northern lands of Scandza. I've sailed south in pursuit of a new life.
I am Fraomar, once a King among my people- the Alemans. Now, in exile. Put a fair purse in my hand and I will see to it that whomever speaks ill of your name shall next meet the end of my sword.
I'm a former military commander, i've served the usurper Procopius, but to my shame, i've betrayed him for Valens. Now i'm trying to lead a life far from imperial politics.
I'm an aspiring warrior from the Suebi tribe. I have a good understanding of logistics and leadership, although i have no practical experience
I'm a veteran targeteer, formerly serving in the army of Valentinianus.
I'm Sela, princess by birth, pirate by trade!
I'm a great warrior and leader, if you respect me as such, we'll get along just fine.
I'm an esteemed noble of the Amal family. As a noble of my house I am skilled on horseback and command, with great prowess with the lance, bow, and sword.
I deal in information. Local lords, crime bosses, merchants - they are all my clients. I know what goes on in town, the best deals at the market, and who goes in and out.
I am a warrior of my people. I grew up in Dacia and Gothia, but have already travelled far in my young age in the employ of the Romans.
I was one of Ulfila's many pupils who helped translate the bible to Gothic
My name is Ulfilas, a Goth and a Christian, humble servant of our lord and his son, Jesus Christ.
I'm the 'bastard' son of Balamber, king of the Huns. After my half-brothers cast me out, i was roaming the steppes alone, until i met you.
I'm a noble from the Onogur clan, but i've left the life of a chieftain behind. Now I'm trying to achieve greatness on the battlefield, without the constant backstabbing by tribal nobility.

I'm a shaman, i've learned about the spiritual realm my entire life. Currently i'm seeking to obtain more earthly skills, so i'll be able to return to my tribe with a balanced knowledge of all walks of life.
I'm a warrior and a raider. During my years in war, i've mastered the art of terror, and now all who know my name tremble in fear. And they are right to be afraid.
I'm a former bandit, adept at riding and archery. I'm looking to make a name for myself as a mercenary.
My name is Visvadeva, merchant by trade. Coin is my passion, and I know how to get it. You’d be foolish not to seek my aid.
I'm a warrior, royal bodyguard and advisor by profession. King Beler has elevated me into nobility, but since we had our disagreements, i'm left without a job.
I'm a noble of Royal Scythian descent. But after making a fatal mistake, i've brought dishonor to my name and now i only wish to leave everything behind and forget about the past.
I'm a horseman who recently lost his steed, i've been looking for work ever since, so i can afford a new horse.
Andeman. I know mountains, and men do what I tell them, and I'm still deciding which of those two is the stranger. Eighteen years old. You'll get used to it.
Arash. Named for the archer who shot the border of the world. I made a shot once that men still talk about. Ask them, not me.
Ardazanes. My father was one of the Immortals. I'll be one, and then I'll command them. Eighteen years old and the best sword west of the Euphrates. Check it yourself, if you like.

Barsumas. Rost-Sohunum, before the Romans had a go at it. I read ground for the King of Kings. Then I watched a Roman army die of its own decisions, and I've been keeping a record of every army that died the same way before it. Ask me about the ground.
Bineses. Highborn once. A prisoner after that. Not much of anything since. I mean to take back what Rome kept from me - under your banner, if the banner's worth it.
Borzmehr. Eighteen years old, and I've been carrying other men's words since I was thirteen. I know every road worth knowing and I'm sick of the sight of all of them.
Eleazar. Born Khorohbut, in Armenia. I kept the King of Kings' accounts until the Romans took me with the baggage. I count, I buy, and I know what things are actually worth. Very little else.
Isdegerdes. I was the second man in the tent when Rome gave up Nisibis, and nobody thought to write that part down. I read enemies, and I do the work other men won't put their name to.
Maruta. A Syriac physician. I gather the dead of Persia and set down what was done to them. I can also keep your living breathing, if that's more use to you.

Mirshabur, out of Ctesiphon. I can put an arrow anywhere on the circle from a moving horse, which counts for nothing at home without a grandfather. I'm making a name loud enough to carry through a palace wall.
I'm a peasant. I'm strong, i'm capable, but never had the opportunity to make something of myself... Until now!
I'm a wandering poet, musician and merchant. I want to share the songs about my journeys.
I'm an adventurer, taking on mercenary or bounty hunting jobs. I've become quite famous around these parts as someone with otherworldly abilities. Although exaggerated, i'm fond of these legends.
I'm a son of Scythian immigrants, decided to join the army to better serve the Empire. There isn't much to my story, at least not yet.
I'm first and foremost a writer, but i have a lot of experience in administration. For many years i've served Rome as governor in Pannonia.
I'm a medical doctor with over a decade of experience in various illnesses. I'm writing a book about chronic and acute maladies.
I am but a humble pilgrim, all i wish for is to walk in the steps of Christ and write a journal about my travels for my congregation back home!
I am a physician, who have served in the court of the Emperor's court for years, under master Priscianus.

I'm a champion of the Olympic games, me and my brother Horus have fought in many arenas all over the empire. Since i've traveled to the west, we have not met, but i'm certain we will meet again in the next Olympic games!
I am Publius Flavius Vegetius Renatus, veteran of the imperial army, expert at military training, tactics and logistics. If you want to know more, read my book, once it's finished.
I'm a noble from Bukhara, after being denied the governor's position, i've been trying to establish a name for myself, to one day return and take my rightful place as the lord of Bukhara.
Yes, yes. The healer must go to where there is need of healing.
The law is the law, and murder is murder.
These are hard times. Don't worry about the fate of outlaws.

My father was a tenant farmer from near Usanc. By law, so long as he paid a third of his crop in tax, he couldn't be kicked off the land. But the landlord wanted to raise sheep, so he had a document forged that said my family moved here a generation ago and therefore wasn't covered by the law... It's a bit complicated, this part, but the end is that they cheated my family of its rights and we were cast into poverty.

There was a woman who lived out on the street. Refugee from the wars. Had a small child, a baby really. It was all she had. She'd make small cakes of wheat over a fire. Then one day a young man from the palace came down the street in his horse. Wasn't looking where he was going, didn't care, and his horse crushed that baby's head.

I fought with the Company of the Boar. I was their armorer - kept their blades sharp, and patched the holes in the mail they took off corpses. Good lads, some of them, but others... Let's just say that it's the kind of outfit that attracts men born to trouble.

Anyway, I couldn't quite go back to the Company after that. His mess-mates knew well enough what happened. So I need work somewhere else. I suppose I could look for work at a smithy, but I don't think I'm cut out for peace. I just want to fight against an enemy in front of me without worrying about the one behind me as well.

There was a great deal of marching to and fro, in the mud, and I shan't bore you with that. But you must have heard of what happened when we caught them. We were forming our ranks to charge when another knight - if indeed he is worthy of the name - told me that I had no place in the front and I must join the second rank of horses.
A warrior stands beside his comrades like a man stands beside his brothers. Whatever their crimes may be.

I kill for a living. I've killed a lot, and if you want me to kill for you, you'll hire me. You seem to have been around a bit. I don't think I need to tell you any more. I'm sure you can reckon if I'm worth my price.
*The strangers eyes do not lift from his manuscripts* Hmm? Yes, can I help you?
*You approach the young stranger; his hands clasped in prayer* Oh, can I help you, sir?
Hello stranger, may I assist you?
Greetings, what do you ask of me, stranger?
Heavens bless you. How might I be of assistance, stranger?
To think this is how a commoner would address royalty. May the Gods blind me and deafen my ears...Since you are listening already, indulge me and listen to my tale, stranger.
Careful. You've put your shadow across mine. Give me a name to hang on you before I choose one myself.

...and the last of the great wild oxen walked north into the fog, and not one man thought to mark the day. A whole kind of creature gone out of the world, and not a line of verse on it. Hm. You're standing there. How long have you been standing there? No - your name first.
Of course, stranger! I was born by the name Setana, but nowadays people only know me as 'The Hound of Culann'.
My name is Torna, you may have heard of me as 'Torna the Sage'.
You're the first through that door in a month who isn't as soft as clotted cream. Sit a moment - Uthyr.
Those men outside - yours, are they? Set them on a flock of sheep and I'd back the sheep. One of them's holding his spear like a broom. Vortigern. And you'd be?

Hail stranger, you’ve the look of a sea-green whelk about you. I am Amarantus, a child of Yisrael, sailor and merchant by trade. For ten years I’ve navigated the coasts of Egypt and Libya, as far as Antioch, and down to Carthage. In my time, I’ve played host to many a weary traveller, not unlike yourself, seeking passage to the southern provinces. Not without a fair share of strife, mind. The seas of the mare Libycum prove treacherous to even the most experienced of sailors.
Questions will come later. First, please take a seat and enjoy wine with me!
You don't bear the look of an Egyptian. From where do you hail?
Tell me, stranger, have you spilt blood in service to Rome?
My name is Horus, I am an Olympian!
My name is Nemota, I am a Roman of great repute from the town of that name in Cyprus.
My name is Oribasius, I’m a physician of renowned quality.
Hail there traveller, might I borrow a moment of your time?
Hah, the balls on this one! So you are not afraid of me like the others here?
Eric is the name my mother gave me, a common name in my tribe; the Suiones of Scandza.
Stop there, stranger, your eyes tell me you have need of a worthy sword-arm.
My name is Gomoar. If you want to hear my story, i will tell you. But this is no heroic tale i'm afraid.
Mhm. Very well. I'm Natuspardo, veteran of many battles.
My name is Andela, an esteemed noble of the Amal family, the clan of Vinitharius himself.
Now, why would I tell a stranger about myself for no reason? Do you know what kind of problems that can put you in?
My name is Gainas, I am a warrior of my people.
My name is Sigesarius, a follower of the teachings of the holy Ulfilas.
My name is Ulfilas, a Goth and a Christian, humble servant of our lord and his son, Jesus Christ.
You should be careful to address me with respect, stranger!
My name is Belar of the Onogur clan.
My friends call me Honagur, my enemies call me 'the Beast'.
My name is Sandeces, at your service!
I bow to you, wearied stranger. Who are you?
Of course, stranger, let's drink a cup of mead together!
I'm Modares, son of Rassogos. My line of ancestry goes back to the times of Royal Scythia.
People always want to know why grown men take orders from me. You'll ask eventually. Andeman - your name first.
You're looking at the bow. They all look at the bow. Go on - ask me my name, and then decide whether you believe it.
Hold a moment - are you a warrior? You've the look of somebody who matters. Ardazanes. And you?
Every captain who comes through here asks what's on the road ahead. Not one of them asks what happened on it. Barsumas. Your name?
Well met, stranger. You've the eyes of someone who has seen much and forgotten little. Your name?
I've carried letters about people like you. None of them flattering. Borzmehr - what's your name?
I'd wager you're paying twice what you should for your company's supplies. Most people are. Sit - Eleazar. And you?
Sit, if you're sitting. You've already decided you don't much like me - that's fine, most people manage it faster. Isdegerdes. And your name?
Your shoulder was set by an amateur. It aches when the weather turns. Sit. I'm Maruta - and you?
You looked at the doors before you looked at the people. So do I. Mirshabur - and you?
Eh? Why do you want to know me of all people?
I'm Sadko, wandering poet, musician and merchant of exotic goods.
I am Aurelius Victor, and I am a servant of Rome. When is an event never auspicious? It is only the miserable and ignorant that do not realize the ability to take advantage of chance.
My name is Caelius Aurelianus. I'm a medical doctor.
My name is Egeria, i'm from a small village from a distant land.
Tell me sir, what do you know of suffering?
I'm Phanes, if you're an enthusiast for the Olympic games, you may have heard of me!
My name is Publius Flavius Vegetius Renatus, but I answer to and prefer Vegetius.
My name is Mavak, nobleman of Bukhara.

We burned away some of the forest and planted barley. My mother died of a fever, but me and my sister and my father, we lived up there 10 lean and lonely years, all so my father didn't have to doff his hat to any other man. Then he vanished in a blizzard.
You ask a lot of questions, friend. So I'll tell you what you need to know, and no more.

I am the son of a knight, but not a son born in wedlock. I was raised in my father's house, but when he was taken prisoner and ransomed, he had to sell much of what he owned, and therefore could no longer support me. I decided to set out to make my own name, if my family could not give me one. It is a common tale.

My father was a wheelwright but there's more money in catapults than in carts these days. I did a bit of work repairing the mangonels round the walls of my hometown, and I reckon I can build some as well.

Well, you know what a man of honor does when he is insulted like that -- I struck him down, and then his friends came against me, and I struck them down too! I laid a full dozen of them down before they finally overbore me. Have you ever heard of a more glorious stand against such odds in the name of honor?
Perhaps I can give you the journeys you seek. Every campfire has need of a good storyteller.
I think your skills could be quite useful in my service. Name your price.
If you seek experience, particularly in martial matters, perhaps you would do well to join me.
Your knowledge of the history of this land is vast, I am certain that having you at my side in diplomatic affairs would be invaluable.
You've seen more conflict than most men care to in a lifetime. Want to see some more?
A priest to guide and heal us would be worth a great sum. I would hope to have you join me.
A Fennid and A Druid in one person. Fascinating. Are you looking for work?
What a tale. So you are looking to make money?
Then come and see where it runs.
Come with me, then. You can tell me the rest on the road.
I can't stay for your lessons, but maybe you could join my companions. We could all benefit from your teachings!
What a fascinating story! Would you be interested in mercenary work?
That's very noble of you! But then, why aren't you with the king?
Then learn from me. Fall in.
Ambition I can use. Come along.
I have need of a capable helmsman in my voyages across the mare Nostrum, I’d pay a fair sum for your talents.
Most impressive. I myself am leading a company of soldiers, and someone of your caliber could be of great value to us.
Come with me, and adventure awaits you.
I am always on the hunt for blooded and noble warriors whose victories outnumber their lived years, your service would be well received in my retinue.
Impressive, a man of your skill would have no trouble in battle.
Impressive, I could use a man of your command talents.
Impressive, I could use a man of your repute and knowledge.
Perhaps I can give you the chance to see the world again, to glance once more at these structures you venerate.
I hope you've learned some actual skills from your teacher!
Impressive, I could use a man with such unique knowledge.
And did your aim find the target?
That's an admirable feat, worthy of a poem!
There certainly are! But you'll need a guide and companions. Incidentally, i'm a leader of a warband.
It seems like you always know the right people to kill!
There are opportunities in this world greater than being a roman citizen. If you are handy with that sword of yours, you may achieve greatness!
The fury of the Alemannic tribes in battle is next to legendary- and I am no stranger to battle. You would be most welcome in my retinue.
Do not let that loyalty go to waste Gomoar, you can still make amends in service for a great cause!
I happen to lead a warband. If i were to accept you, what skills could you offer?
I suppose much of those bodies were from your side...
Perhaps. How many pirates are in your company?
Indeed! Any commander would be thankful with such a warrior at their side!
You clearly are a man of great prestige, have you fought these barbarians yourself?
Hmm, do you need any help?
You have clearly done well for yourself as a soldier then.
I’m not familiar with these teachings, but I do not see any reason for you to be persecuted for your faith.
You clearly have many connections and a great deal of influence with the church and the imperial court
No son should be treated this way. But you still have the opportunity to make a name for yourself, on your own merits.
But your tribe is still in the middle of conquest, how are you going to achieve triumphs if you leave the war behind?
I know about the role of Shamans. I just question how could a young man such as yourself have the widom to be trusted with such responsibility?
That seems to be an effective strategy. But wouldn't it backfire if the enemy champion bests you?
A capable young man like you can always find his place in an army!
Truly a sad tale. Your knowledge of the local markets could come in handy.
You're not much of a talker, are you?
I suspect you are no longer in the service of the king. What happened?
Then maybe the best course of action would be to leave these lands forever.
Surely you must have other skills you could utilize in the army!
Then start with mine. Come on.
Then draw for me, and we'll find out which it is.
Then stop saying it and come show me.
I've a war, and I could use a man who's already lost one. Ride with me.
Then get off the hillside. Ride with me.
Then keep my books. Come with me.
I don't care how a thing gets done. Come along.
Then walk with me. You'll get where you're going.
Then earn it. Ride with me.
Someone of your strength could become a great warrior with training, if you join the army!
Thank you Sadko, maybe later. You seem to have experience that may be useful for a travelling warband.
But aren't you misleading the public with this performance?
I know what I can accomplish, but what of you? What can you provide in place of a sword?
I have my own methods of fighting my enemies, but as a leader of a company, i see the merit in your approach!
I'd gladly help you on your way, but i'm leading a warband, and i can't guarantee your safety at all times.
With such a prestigious honor, why are you concerned with my company? What can you offer?
I'm a great admirer of Olympic athletes! I'm honored to meet a champion such as you!
Impressive. I could use a man of your experience!
You path isn't set, Mavak! You can still forge your own destiny!
I would have little use for one of your talents. When I have need of a court scribe, I will seek you out.
Palaces and great towers are a fine thing, but in battle I need someone who can hold their own, not erect a wall to hide behind.
Although you may learn much in my service, I have little time to teach you in the intricate affairs of warfare.
I have met many historians in my time, and seen many of them in battle. They do not fare well.
You're an experienced warrior and leader of men, that much is clear. If ever I have need of such a man, I'll know where to look.
I do not care so deeply for the affairs of the spirit, and I fear a priest would be ill-placed on the field of battle.
Don't think that i'd believe a single word about your prophecies, but you look like a capable fighter
Brooding drunkenly in taverns won't help you reclaim your lands...
You're sixty at the most, old man. Sell that to someone drunker.
I have no interest in your lessons, only your skills. Can you handle yourself in real combat, outside your training grounds?
I care not for your name, but your skills. Would you be interested in mercenary work?
Sounds like a spurious tale. If you're such a hero, why are you in smokey taverns instead of the royal keep?
Big talk from a boy with a borrowed name.
You'd cut my throat the day it suited you. No.
A twice-cursed sailor would be an ill omen in my journeys, I should think. Perhaps you should seek employ elsewhere.
This cannot be. Any man can make such claims!
Desert your post if you like. You'll do it without me.
I fear that your ignoble birth would be a point of fierce discontent among my upper ranks, and I would not have your presence give cause for dissent.
Right, well I’ve never heard of you.
If I wanted to be lectured, I would have gone to the campidoctor.
If I wanted to be lectured, I would have gone to Alexandria.
Forgive me, but I cannot burden myself with an aged man whose prime is long since past, this world is vast and dangerous, and I need people I can count on.
If that's good enough for your school, how can i be certain that your skills are any better?
It sounds like you’ve polluted alchemica with gnostic heresy.
That doesn't sound credible at all...
I'm a worthy opponent! I'd challenge you if i wasn't looking for a warrior like yourself for my party.
If you use your sword for slaying your enemies, rather than your kin, you may atone for this great sin.
Warriors and plunderers do well in my ranks, but to play host to a man once crowned as King? I think not.
You're a coward Gomoar. Simply hiding from your responsibilities won't lift your shame!
You are but a whelp, boy! What use would you be of a commander?
But you've triumphed! Casualties are expected in war...
Come on girl, you take me for a fool? If you're a 'captain', where are yopur pirates?
You strike me as a competent fellow, but an arrogant one!
Why should I care about the plight of some nation of pale and effeminate barbarians in the north?
It sounds like you brought this on yourself.
I’d resent those around me for holding me back in such circumstances, why should I expect you to be loyal?
I’m not too keen on having those condemned as heretics among my entourage.
You’re not even a proper bishop, how are you useful to me?
You can't expect to be treated as royalty if you're just a bastard! You have to man up and carve out your own destiny!
You are responsible for the fate of your family, you can't abandon them just because you dislike politics!
Sounds like nonsense to me. You don't strike me as one with otherworldly knowledge...
Just because you are tall and ugly, doesn't make you a beast. You can be cut down like anyone else.
A former bandit might have the skills to join a warband, if they don't impale you first!
Perhaps I would take pity on you, had you not been making eyes at my purse all this time.
Has the cat got your tongue?
If you're such a trusted bodyguard, why aren't you guarding the king right now?
You'll have to live with this shame for the rest of your life.
A real warrior doesn't need a horse to be effective in combat!
Eighteen years old and handing out orders. Not to mine.
Come back when you can do it twice.
Best sword west of the Euphrates. Just watch out for elephants.

A loosely organized kingdom situated along the bends of the Don and the Volga, the Alans have dwelled in these pastures for centuries after being driven westward from the Kazakh steppes by the Sogdians. Now the Alans once again face the loss of their home as they are beset by another ancient Empire: a people who once called themselves the Xiongnu. As their kingdom collapses, the Alans prepare to mount a last stand against these invaders with their newfound allies in the Greuthungians.

The Kingdom of Armenia often served as a client state or vassal at the frontier of the two large empires and their successors, the Byzantine and Sassanid empires. In 301, Tiridates III proclaimed Christianity as the state religion of Armenia, making the Armenian kingdom the first state in history to embrace Christianity officially.

In 252, Caucasian Albania acknowledged the suzerainty of the Sasanian Empire, appearing among its provinces in Shapur I's inscriptions. The kingdom would remain an integral part of the empire until its fall. By the end of the 3rd-century, the kings of Arran were replaced with an Arsacid family.

It has been ten years since the accession of Rome’s co-emperors, Valentinian and Valens. In the east, the Arian emperor Valens has maintained stability, while his religious tolerance has brought widespread support for his rule. Now, the Romans of Constantinople face their greatest challenge yet: the Sasanians are threatening a war over Roman violations of the treaty, while the Danubian peoples are being pushed into the Empire by an unknown power from the far East.

A broad group of people speaking an Indo-Iranian language, the jazygs have dwelled on the Eurasian steppes for nearly eight centuries now. Although the most poerful jazyg kingdom is that of the Jazyges of Pannonia, some tribes have remained in the pontic steppes.
The Kingdom Kartli existed during Classical Antiquity and the Early Middle Ages, either as an independent state or as a dependent of larger empires, notably the Sassanid and Roman empires.

Localized on the western part of the Caucasus, Lazican tribes have been living under the rule of the roman empire since the collapse of the kingdom of Colchis. By the mid-3rd century, Lazica was given partial autonomy within the Roman Empire and developed into a kingdom.

A broad group of people speaking an Indo-Iranian language, the Sarmatians have dwelled on the Eurasian steppes for nearly eight centuries now. Although the most poerful sarmatian kingdom is that of the Jazyges of Pannonia, some tribes have remained in the pontic steppes.

It has been ten years since the accession of Rome’s co-emperors, Valentinian and Valens. In the west, Valentinian’s adept leadership has quashed usurpations, improved the Empire’s infrastructure, and benefitted the population of the empire as a whole. Now, the empire stands at a precipice: Valentinian’s blindness to the excesses of his officials has resulted in rampant corruption and disloyalty, while Pannonia has been ravaged by the Quadians, incensed at the Roman assassination of their king.

The Sturgians come from the northern woods, just south of the icy Byalic Sea. For centuries they lived an isolated existence in the dark forests, their numbers kept in check by the deadly winters. But as the Empire expanded to fill out the Calradian continent, traders ventured into the woods in search of honey, bog iron, and most of all fur. Great towns sprung up on the network of bays and lakes that joined the Sturgian lands to the outside world, attracting fortune-seekers from the coast, the steppes, and the Nordlands. The princes and boyars of this land have now begun to turn their eyes outward, earning themselves for a reputation for their warlike approach to business and their businesslike approach to war.
Founded on the ruins of Jerusalem, Aelia Capitolina remained but a minor town until the fourth century, when it became a prominent Christian center.
Weathered stone altars crown this windswept rise. Ancient geographers said they marked the farthest reach of Alexander's conquests, where the known world gave way to the lands beyond.
An ancient Dolmen and nearby burial mound at the coast of Cimbria.
The broken statue of the god Helios at the harbour of Rhodus, once a mighty wonder of the world...
A massive ramparts-and-ditches fortification system, protecting the territory of the Jazyges.
You approach a sacred grove with a large oak tree, dedicated to the god Donar. A place of worship and social gathering for many tribes beyond the Rhenus river.
A large mound on the steppes, near the foothills of the Caucasus Mountains.

According to the Roman tradition, Vulcan the god of blacksmithing, had his forge under Mount Aetna. It is said that whenever his wife, the godess Venus is unfaithful, Vulcan grows angry and beats the red-hot metal with such a force that sparks and smoke rose up from the top of the mountain...
A sacred grove dedicated to the twin elk-gods, called Alcis.
A sacred grove dedicated to the germanic goddess Baduhenna, near to an ancient battlefield, where the Frisians defeated a Roman legion in 28 AD.
A sacred grove of the germanic Semnones, near the Viadrus river.
You stand before the great wall of Emperor Hadrianus, that once protected the province of Britannia. The fortifications still stand strong, but the civilian settlements are ruined and abandoned...

The legendary Hanging Gardens of Babylon, one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. As you approach the famous Ishtar Gate, you see the fabulously ornamented terraces of the gardens in the distance.
A great carved wooden Pillar, erected and worshipped beneath the open sky by the local germanic tribes.
The famous lighthouse of Alexandria, a true wonder of the world. It is believed to be the tallest tower in existence.

The renowned monumental tomb, raised in the town of Halicarnassus to be the resting place of Mausolus a satrap in the Achaemenid Persian Empire, and his sister-wife Artemisia II. You see the Mausoleum towering over the surrounding buildings, decorated with reliefs and sculptures.
On the summit of the Taurus Mountains stands a tomb-sanctuary, flanked by terraces with huge statues.
An exceptionally grand circular mound, with a facade made of white cobblestones and ringed by engraved kerbstones. It is believed to have been used for burials in ages past.
An impressive burial mound, next to the river Borysthenes. According to the locals, it's the resting place of Scythian kings.
The most ancient of the seven wonders of the world, the monumental Pyramids stand tall as a reminder of the greatness of Egyptian civilization.
Necropolis of the Persian Kings, carved into the arid cliffside, featuring several Achaemenid royal tombs, as well as rock reliefs of Sassanid kings.
A large mound, standing tall in the surrounding flat plains.
Standing on top of a mountain, a few standing stones mark the location of an ancient ritual site.

The sanctuary of Olympia is a sacred site of the hellenic world, where every four years athletic competitions are held in honor of Zeus, the king of the gods. The immense chryselephantine sculpture of Zeus is in the center of the sactuary.

A massive alignment of thousands of standing stones. According to local legend, each of the stones were once pagan soldiers who had been turned into stone by the Christian Pope Cornelius over a hundred years ago.
A monumental ancient temple, dedicated to the Godess Artemis, or Diana, as known by the romans, near the city of Ephesus.

An old lighthouse, known as the Farum Brigantium. According to myth, the hero Hercules slew the giant tyrant Geryon after three days and three nights of battle. The lighthouse, standing atop a skull and crossbones representing the buried head of Hercules' slain enemy.
An old Bridge, built by Emperor Traianus centuries ago, it's believed to be the longest bridge in the world. The wooden structure is ruined, but the stone foundation stands strong.
An old, overgrown victory monument of a certain roman general called Nero Claudius Drusus, commemorating his victories over the local tribes.

In 324, the ancient city of Byzantium was renamed New Rome and declared the new capital of the Roman Empire by Emperor Constantine the Great. On 11 May 330, it was renamed to Constantinople, and dedicated to Constantine.[6] Constantinople is generally considered to be the center and the cradle of Orthodox Christian civilization. From the mid-5th century, Constantinople was the largest and wealthiest city in Europe.

The Roman city was established in 177 BC by Publius Aelius, Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and Gnaeus Sicinius. It was a military stronghold for the campaigns against the Ligures. In the 5th century, it was still notable, as it was chosen as the seat of a bishopric.

Mediolanum, the Latinized form of Medhelanon, was conquered by the Romans in 222 B.C. due to its strategic position on the northern borders of the Empire. When Diocletian decided to divide the Empire in half choosing the Eastern half for himself, Milan became the residence of Maximian, ruler of the Western Roman Empire. The beginning of the 5th century was the start of a tortuous period of barbarian invasions for Mediolanum. After the city was besieged by the Visigoths in 402, the imperial residence was moved to Ravenna.

The most believed hypothesis is that the origin of the name Pisa comes from Etruscan and mean 'mouth', as Pisa is at the mouth of the Arno river. During the last years of the Western Roman Empire, Pisa did not decline as much as the other cities of Italia, probably due to the complexity of its river system and its consequent ease of defence.

Placentia was founded as Roman military colonies in May 218 BC. Although sacked and devastated several times, the city always recovered and by the 6th century Procopius was calling it the principal city in the country of Aemilia.

Jaculan sits in the warmer southern reaches of the Biscan coast, in rolling hills known for their olive trees. It was once a favored resort of the imperial aristocracy, who hunted wild boars amid the oak forests. The independent peasantry of this region are known for their heterodox ideas. The Brotherhood of the Woods is but the latest of a series of rebellions to have broken out here, sometimes aided by an aristocracy that considers them a tool to use against rival Vlandian houses.

Ravenna greatly prospered under Roman rule. During the Marcomannic Wars, Germanic settlers in Ravenna revolted and managed to seize possession of the city. For this reason, Marcus Aurelius decided not only against bringing more barbarians into Italia, but even banished those who had previously been brought there. In AD 408, Emperor Honorius transferred the capital of the Western Roman Empire from Rome to Ravenna; it subsequently served as the capital of the empire for most period of the 5th century and the last de facto western emperor Romulus Augustulus was deposed here in AD 476.

Though declining slowly through the years, Syracuse maintained the status of capital of the Roman government of Sicily and seat of the praetor. It remained an important port for trade between the Eastern and the Western parts of the Empire.
During the late Republic and all the Roman Empire, Tarentum was a simple provincial city

In the first century BC (probably 28 BC), the Romans founded Augusta Taurinorum. After the fall of the Western Roman Empire, the town, along with the rest of the Italian peninsula, was conquered by the Heruli and the Ostrogoths.

The precise details of Verona's early history remain a mystery along with the origin of the name. The city became important because it was at the intersection of several roads. Stilicho defeated Alaric and his Visigoths here in 403.
A town in Syria, named after the legendary Palmyrene Queen.
